settlements.name: Calder
settlements.why: Bedrock island at the mouth of the Tennalee, beside the deepest natural water in Cassena Sound; head of ocean navigation and the first dry, defensible ground below the falls.

settlements.name: Tennalee Falls
settlements.why: Fall-line mill town where the Tennalee drops over granite ledges into tidewater; water power, then the railroad crossing.

settlements.name: Riverside
settlements.why: Low terrace on the east bank of the Tennalee mouth facing downtown Calder; barge wharves, rail junction and the old ferry landing.

settlements.name: Halcomb Heights
settlements.why: Foothill ridges above the North Channel that became commuter suburbs once the Tennalee River Bridge opened.

settlements.name: Corliss
settlements.why: Worker town on the higher western end of a flat delta-and-spoil island whose east end holds the port, refinery and yards.

settlements.name: Bellamy Bluffs
settlements.why: Sandy bluffs at the south end of the Long Bridge; suburbs grew between the interstate landing and the airport.

settlements.name: Coldwater
settlements.why: County seat in the middle of the limestone Coldwater Valley at the junction of the valley road, the railroad and the plateau road.

settlements.name: Narrows Landing
settlements.why: Bridgehead where the Narrows is narrowest and the Coldwater Valley meets the strait.

settlements.name: Ledford
settlements.why: Gateway town where the Gap Road leaves the coastal foothills and starts up the Ledford Prong toward the crest.

settlements.name: Shady Gap
settlements.why: Low saddle between the Coldwater Valley and the south coast used by the interstate and railroad; truck stops and a rail siding.

settlements.name: Hominy
settlements.why: Head of Hominy Bay, the only sheltered anchorage on the island's southwest coast.

settlements.name: Hickory Flat
settlements.why: Plateau-top crossroads on the Hickory Tableland, flat enough for an airport and dry enough for a town.

settlements.name: Calloway
settlements.why: Lake village on the east shore of Calloway Lake, built around the marinas and the dam construction camp site.

settlements.name: Upper Cove
settlements.why: Farm hamlet on the flat floor of the upper Tennalee Cove, above the reservoir's full-pool line.

settlements.name: Big Laurel
settlements.why: North-coast cove at the mouth of Big Laurel Creek; the only landing on the steep North Face.

settlements.name: Pigeonroost
settlements.why: Where the Gap Road reaches the Narrows at the mouth of Pigeonroost Creek.

settlements.name: Graystone
settlements.why: Ferry and quarry town on the island's one sheltered south-facing harbor, between the Thunderhole mouth and Quarry Creek.

settlements.name: Fallon
settlements.why: Harbor in the only cove breaking the Fallon Cliffs; fishing boats and the Coast Guard station.

settlements.name: Whitlock
settlements.why: Summer village on the cool highland plateau beside Lake Whitlock, 1,050 m above the sound.

settlements.name: Cutstone
settlements.why: Quarry village beside the granite pit on Cutstone Mountain.

settlements.name: Bright Water
settlements.why: Mill village where the Bright Water River leaves the foot of the Blue Wall.

settlements.name: Stillhouse
settlements.why: Fishing hamlet at the mouth of Stillhouse Branch on the north shore.

settlements.name: Bellamy
settlements.why: Courthouse town in the middle of the farm plain where the state highways and the shortline railroad cross the Ocosta.

settlements.name: Harlow
settlements.why: Red Hills market village near the kaolin pits.

settlements.name: Kinard
settlements.why: Crossroads and grain elevator on the railroad between Bellamy and the Ashwood River bridge.

settlements.name: Ocosta
settlements.why: River landing at the head of the Ocosta estuary, the old limit of tidewater barge traffic.

settlements.name: Sweetwater
settlements.why: Farm hamlet on Sweetwater Creek.

settlements.name: Dunmore
settlements.why: Flatwoods hamlet on the road to the Wickham ferry.

settlements.name: Mirabel Beach
settlements.why: Widest stretch of the barrier island, directly across Mirabel Sound from the causeway landing.

settlements.name: Dunewood
settlements.why: Planned beach village on the high dune section south of Mirabel Beach.

settlements.name: Port Serena
settlements.why: Marina town on the sheltered lagoon side of the beach-ridge foreland, near the south bridge.

settlements.name: Seaholly
settlements.why: North-end village by the pass into Cassena Sound.

settlements.name: Haversham
settlements.why: The highest bluff on the island fronting the deepest tidal river: dry ground beside a natural deep-water landing, central to the island's farmland.

settlements.name: Ambrose Beach
settlements.why: Holocene barrier beach reached by the causeway across the Bonnet River marsh.

settlements.name: Oyster Point
settlements.why: Shrimping village on Oyster Hammock, the closest high ground to the Corliss fish market.

settlements.name: Edgewater
settlements.why: Village on the sea-island core across the Haversham River from town.

settlements.name: Kettle
settlements.why: Hamlet on Kettle Island, the southern sea-island core, where the coastal highway leaves for Ketch Sound.

settlements.name: Rice Hope
settlements.why: Farm hamlet on the edge of the old rice-field impoundments.

settlements.name: Wickham
settlements.why: Store, church and a few houses on the dry rise above Seacow Spring, where the island road ends.

settlements.name: Cedar Shoals
settlements.why: Fish houses on pilings at Cedar Point, the island's only harbor.

settlements.name: Wickham Landing
settlements.why: Ferry slip on the north shore facing Bellamy.

settlements.name: Ossahatchee
settlements.why: Dry ground at the north end of Long Ridge where the coastal highway lands from Ketch Sound and the Trail turns west into the swamp.

settlements.name: Tarrow Landing
settlements.why: Ferry and seaplane landing where Long Ridge comes closest to Tarrow Sound.

settlements.name: Tolar
settlements.why: Remnant sawmill hamlet on a pine island along the Trail.

settlements.name: Sabal Landing
settlements.why: Mainland end of the Keys bridges on the marsh coast.

settlements.name: Kestrel
settlements.why: Widest part of Kestrel Island, sheltered behind the big dunes.

settlements.name: Merrin
settlements.why: Maritime-forest village at the elbow of Cape Merrin with a sound-side harbor.

settlements.name: Pennick
settlements.why: Ferry-only village on the widest part of Pennick Island.

settlements.name: Shellbank
settlements.why: Fishing hamlet beside Sheepshead Inlet.

settlements.name: Sabal
settlements.why: Fishing village on the largest key, at the end of the Keys bridges.

settlements.name: Cayo Viento
settlements.why: Stilt-house hamlet on the windward key.

bridges.name: Long Bridge
bridges.type: low trestle with high-rise navigation hump

bridges.name: Sawpit Pass Bridge
bridges.type: steel swing span on timber approaches

helipads.name: Ledford Dome Ranger Pad
helipads.note: gravel pad beside the summit lot

utilities.name: Bellamy Peanut Shellers and Cotton Gin

plants.name: Corliss Generating Station
plants.kind: gas combined-cycle with two retired coal stacks

plants.name: Ocosta Nuclear Station
plants.kind: two-unit pressurized-water reactor with hyperbolic cooling towers

landmarks.name: Ledford Dome Tower
landmarks.desc: A concrete observation tower with a spiral ramp on the highest summit in the islands, rising just above the spruce–fir canopy.
landmarks.why: Built where the archipelago's highest point is hidden by trees.
landmarks.look: A pale disc on a ramp, on top of a black conifer dome.
landmarks.near: Ledford Dome Road, Ledford Spruce–Fir Forest, Ledford Gap.
landmarks.memorable: The point from which every other landmark in the islands can be seen.

landmarks.name: Callahan North Face
landmarks.desc: The 1,900 m north face of Mount Callahan rising from the Narrows, with pale slate cliffs in its upper third.
landmarks.why: The strait has cut into the base of the steepest mountain front in the islands.
landmarks.look: A wall of forest and rock filling the view from the mainland.
landmarks.near: Mount Callahan, Narrows Road, Big Laurel.
landmarks.memorable: Snow and rime on its cliffs above a sea strait.

landmarks.name: Calder Tower
landmarks.desc: A 64-storey glass tower with a stepped crown and a lit spire, the tallest building in the islands.
landmarks.why: Built on the bedrock bluff at the heart of Downtown.
landmarks.look: Blue-green glass by day, a white lit crown by night.
landmarks.memorable: Visible from the Ledford Dome tower 22 km away.

landmarks.name: Gate Bridge
landmarks.desc: A suspension bridge with a 1,020 m main span strung between cliff-top towers, its deck 190 m above Hollow Reach. On the Halcomb side the road leaves the Bearpen Tunnel straight onto the bridge.
landmarks.why: The narrowest point of the drowned gorge, with rock both sides.
landmarks.look: Two grey towers and a thin deck between granite walls.
landmarks.near: Bearpen Tunnel, Veil Falls, Gate Shelf, Blue Wall Road.
landmarks.memorable: Cars emerging from a tunnel directly onto a bridge in the sky.

landmarks.name: Grayback Mountain
landmarks.desc: A bare granite dome rising 380 m out of the farmland of the Piedmont strip.
landmarks.why: A resistant granite pluton.
landmarks.look: Grey whaleback against the green.
landmarks.memorable: The island is named after it.

landmarks.name: Lantern Mountain Radar Dome
landmarks.desc: A white air-traffic radar dome and lit tower on the second-highest summit of Graystone.
landmarks.why: Clear radar coverage over the sea and all the islands.
landmarks.look: A white golf ball on the skyline.
landmarks.memorable: Its red lights pulse over the north coast at night.

landmarks.name: Corliss Stacks
landmarks.desc: Two 180 m concrete chimneys of the old coal units at the Corliss Generating Station, with red-and-white bands near the top.
landmarks.why: Tall stacks to disperse smoke over the sound, beside the cooling water.
landmarks.look: Twin banded chimneys above the port.
landmarks.near: Corliss Generating Station, Cooling Pond, Landfill Hill.
landmarks.memorable: Seen from Graystone, Saint Ambrose and Calder alike.

landmarks.name: Ocosta Cooling Towers
landmarks.desc: Two hyperbolic concrete cooling towers of the nuclear station, usually trailing white plumes.
landmarks.why: Cooling water from Ketch Sound and the flat, stable ground of south Bellamy.
landmarks.look: Two hourglass towers and their steam clouds.
landmarks.near: Ocosta Nuclear Station, Clearwater Bay, Ocosta estuary.
landmarks.memorable: The plumes are visible from Wickham, Ossahatchee and Mirabel.

landmarks.name: WCDR-TV Mast
landmarks.desc: A guyed television mast 518 m tall, the tallest structure in the islands, with banks of red lights.
landmarks.why: Flat farmland lets a single tall mast cover all the islands.
landmarks.look: A needle on the horizon with blinking red lights.
landmarks.memorable: Its lights are visible from nearly everywhere at night.

landmarks.name: Cape Merrin Lighthouse
landmarks.desc: A brick lighthouse 60 m tall painted in a diagonal black-and-white checkerboard, the tallest light on the coast.
landmarks.why: Marks the cape and the long Merrin Shoals extending offshore.
landmarks.look: Checkered tower above the maritime forest.
landmarks.memorable: Its beam sweeps over the breakers on the shoals.

landmarks.name: Merrin Shoals Wind Farm
landmarks.desc: Twenty-eight offshore wind turbines in rows on the shallow shoals east of the Banks.
landmarks.why: Shallow water and steady wind on the shoals.
landmarks.look: White turbines on the ocean horizon.
landmarks.memorable: Red lights blinking in unison at night.

landmarks.name: Calloway Dam
landmarks.desc: A 135 m concrete gravity dam in the quartzite gorge below Tennalee Cove, with a road across its crest and a powerhouse at its foot.
landmarks.why: The gorge narrows between quartzite ridges here, the cheapest place to hold back the river.
landmarks.look: A pale concrete wall between wooded ridges.
landmarks.near: Calloway Lake, Hogback, Calloway Dam Road.
landmarks.memorable: Standing on the crest with lake on one side and gorge on the other.

landmarks.name: Long Bridge
landmarks.desc: A low concrete trestle carrying I-21 across the sound to Bellamy, rising to a high navigation hump in the middle.
landmarks.why: The shortest crossing from Calder to the flat land for the airport.
landmarks.look: A long line on the water with a hump.
landmarks.near: Bellamy Bluffs, South Shore, Ashwood River mouth.
landmarks.memorable: The hump framing the skyline.

landmarks.name: Narrows Bridge
landmarks.desc: A steel cantilever truss carrying I-21 from the mainland across the narrowest point of the Narrows.
landmarks.why: The Narrows is narrowest where the Coldwater Valley meets the strait.
landmarks.look: Black steel truss against the North Face.
landmarks.near: Narrows Landing, Narrows Rail Bridge, Narrows crossing towers.
landmarks.memorable: The gateway to the islands.

landmarks.name: The Blue Wall
landmarks.desc: The escarpment along the south-east side of the Graystone highlands, falling 800 m in two kilometres, streaked with waterfalls.
landmarks.why: The edge of the uplifted highland block, being worn back by the rain-soaked streams.
landmarks.look: A blue-hazed wall across the island.
landmarks.near: Glassface Dome, Pale Wall, Thunderhole Falls, Anvil Rock.
landmarks.memorable: Seen from Calder as a blue rampart behind Graystone.

landmarks.name: Fallon Cliffs
landmarks.desc: Granite sea cliffs up to 250 m high along Graystone's east coast, with the Coast Road running along the top.
landmarks.why: The highlands meet the open Atlantic and the waves undercut them.
landmarks.look: Pink-grey walls rising out of the surf.
landmarks.near: Coast Road, Fallon, Cape Fallon Light.
landmarks.memorable: Breakers exploding at the foot of the cliffs.

landmarks.name: Corliss Gantry Cranes
landmarks.desc: Eight ship-to-shore container cranes lined along the berth, their booms raised when idle.
landmarks.why: Deep berth beside the ship channel.
landmarks.look: Red and white cranes like giant animals.
landmarks.memorable: Raised booms silhouetted at sunset.

landmarks.name: Calder Heights Tower
landmarks.desc: A self-supporting broadcast tower on the summit of Calder Heights.
landmarks.why: The highest ground in the city.
landmarks.look: A lattice tower above the reservoir.
landmarks.memorable: Lit in different colours for holidays.

landmarks.name: Mirabel Sands
landmarks.desc: The tallest condominium tower on the barrier island, white with curved balconies.
landmarks.why: Beachfront at the widest part of the island.
landmarks.look: A white slab above the strip.
landmarks.memorable: It glows pink at sunset.

landmarks.name: Narrows Crossing Towers
landmarks.desc: A pair of 150 m transmission towers carrying high-voltage lines across the Narrows.
landmarks.why: The power line from the mainland must clear shipping in the strait.
landmarks.look: Red-and-white towers with wires sagging across the water.
landmarks.memorable: Wires humming over the strait.

landmarks.name: Tennalee River Bridge
landmarks.desc: The interstate bridge from Halcomb into Calder across the North Channel.
landmarks.why: The shortest crossing west of Downtown.
landmarks.look: A long concrete arc above the channel.
landmarks.memorable: Where the skyline first appears.

landmarks.name: Kestrel Hill Dune
landmarks.desc: A 28 m bare migrating sand dune.
landmarks.why: Wind-blown sand piles up where the barrier is widest.
landmarks.look: A white hill on a flat island.
landmarks.memorable: Visible from the inlet bridges and from boats offshore.

landmarks.name: Veil Falls
landmarks.desc: Hollow Creek leaps 130 m from the rim of Hollow Reach straight into the sea, spreading into spray.
landmarks.why: The creek has not cut down as fast as the drowned gorge, so it falls from a hanging valley.
landmarks.look: A white veil on a dark granite wall.
landmarks.near: Veil Falls Shingle, Gate Bridge, Hawkbill Knob.
landmarks.memorable: Visible from the Gate Bridge deck four kilometres away.

landmarks.name: Thunderhole Falls
landmarks.desc: The Thunderhole River drops 120 m in a series of falls through a slot in the Blue Wall.
landmarks.why: The river crosses the escarpment in a narrow gorge.
landmarks.look: White water in a dark slot.
landmarks.memorable: Its roar can be heard from the Whitlock Grade.

landmarks.name: Hickory Falls
landmarks.desc: An 80 m free-falling waterfall where Hickory Creek leaves the Tableland.
landmarks.why: The creek flows over the hard sandstone caprock and falls where it ends.
landmarks.look: A thin plunge into a deep amphitheatre.
landmarks.memorable: Behind the falls is a rock shelter you can walk into.

landmarks.name: Piney Falls
landmarks.desc: Piney Creek falls 85 m from the Tableland Bluffs onto the cobbles of Piney Cove.
landmarks.why: The sea is cutting the bluffs back faster than the creek can cut down.
landmarks.look: A white thread on the cliffs above the bay.
landmarks.memorable: Seen from boats on Serena Bay.

landmarks.name: Tennalee Falls
landmarks.desc: A broad series of granite ledges where the Tennalee drops into tidewater, between brick mill buildings.
landmarks.why: The fall line, where hard crystalline rock meets softer coastal sediments.
landmarks.look: Wide white water between brick walls.
landmarks.memorable: Kayakers playing in the standing waves below the mills.

landmarks.name: Calder Central Clock Tower
landmarks.desc: The granite clock tower of the main railroad station.
landmarks.why: The passenger railroad's terminus.
landmarks.look: A stone campanile with a lit clock face.
landmarks.memorable: Its chimes heard across Downtown.

landmarks.name: Market Street Bridge
landmarks.desc: A double-deck vertical lift bridge with tall steel towers, carrying road on top and rail beneath.
landmarks.why: Barges must pass up the river to Tennalee Falls.
landmarks.look: Two steel towers lifting a span.
landmarks.memorable: The span rising for a barge.

landmarks.name: Corliss Lift Bridge
landmarks.desc: A 5.6 km rail trestle with a vertical lift span over the ship channel.
landmarks.why: The freight railroad has to cross the ship channel to reach the port.
landmarks.look: Two lift towers in the middle of the water.
landmarks.memorable: Freight trains waiting for ships.

landmarks.name: Harbor Bridge
landmarks.desc: A steel girder bridge with a bascule span carrying I-121 across the Inner Harbor.
landmarks.why: The port spur from the city.
landmarks.look: Steel bascule leaves raised for tugs.
landmarks.memorable: Traffic stopping for the drawspan.

landmarks.name: Cape Fallon Light
landmarks.desc: A short white tower on the cliff-top at the north arm of Fallon Cove.
landmarks.why: The cliffs already give height; a short tower is enough.
landmarks.look: A white tower on dark cliffs.
landmarks.memorable: Its light at the top of a cliff.

landmarks.name: Cape Serena Light
landmarks.desc: A black-and-white banded iron lighthouse on the tip of the foreland.
landmarks.why: Marks the cape and Serena Pass.
landmarks.look: Banded tower over the beach ridges.
landmarks.near: Cape Serena Beach, Long Swale Lake.
landmarks.memorable: The light over the dune lakes.

landmarks.name: Mirabel Pier
landmarks.desc: A 450 m concrete fishing pier with a T-head and a bait shop.
landmarks.why: Built to reach past the surf zone.
landmarks.look: Pilings marching into green water.
landmarks.memorable: Lights reflecting in the sea at night.

landmarks.name: Haversham Steeples
landmarks.desc: Three white church steeples rising above the oaks of Haversham.
landmarks.why: The town on the highest bluff.
landmarks.look: Three white spires above the marsh.
landmarks.memorable: The first sight of the town from the marsh.

landmarks.name: Ambrose Inlet Bridge
landmarks.desc: A high-rise concrete bridge over the inlet between Saint Ambrose and the Banks.
landmarks.why: Inlet must stay open for boats.
landmarks.look: A concrete arc over shoals.
landmarks.memorable: The gateway to the Banks.

landmarks.name: Sabal Bridges
landmarks.desc: A chain of low concrete trestles hopping across the flats to Sabal Key.
landmarks.why: Shallow flats allow low bridges.
landmarks.look: Low bridges over clear water.
landmarks.memorable: Water colour changing under the bridges.

landmarks.name: Ossahatchee Skyway
landmarks.desc: A four-kilometre viaduct carrying the Trail over the swamp, built to let water flow under the road.
landmarks.why: The old causeway blocked the swamp's slow flow.
landmarks.look: A concrete ribbon through treetops.
landmarks.memorable: Driving through the canopy.

landmarks.name: Big Water Tower
landmarks.desc: A wooden observation tower over the open water of Big Water.
landmarks.why: The best view over the swamp.
landmarks.look: A wooden tower over cypress.
landmarks.memorable: Alligators below.

landmarks.name: Highpine Fire Tower
landmarks.desc: A steel fire tower on Long Ridge.
landmarks.why: Fire watch over the swamp.
landmarks.look: Steel tower above longleaf.
landmarks.memorable: The swamp to the horizon.

landmarks.name: Scrub Hill Fire Tower
landmarks.desc: A steel fire tower on Wickham's highest point.
landmarks.why: Fire watch over the longleaf.
landmarks.look: Tower over white sand.
landmarks.memorable: Both coasts in view.

landmarks.name: Gooseberry Fire Tower
landmarks.desc: A fire lookout cab on Gooseberry Bald.
landmarks.why: Watches the valley and the plateau.
landmarks.look: Glass cab on steel legs.
landmarks.memorable: Sunset over the Tableland.

landmarks.name: Cutstone Quarry
landmarks.desc: Terraced granite benches cut into Cutstone Mountain, with a flooded lower pit and old derricks.
landmarks.why: Fine granite close to the harbour.
landmarks.look: Grey stepped benches.
landmarks.memorable: Derrick masts on the rim.

landmarks.name: Coldwater Limestone Quarry
landmarks.desc: A large working limestone quarry with crushers and conveyors on the valley's east side.
landmarks.why: Limestone of the valley floor near the interstate and railroad.
landmarks.look: Pale benches and dust plumes.
landmarks.memorable: Blasting horns echoing across the valley.

landmarks.name: Corliss Landfill Hill
landmarks.desc: A capped landfill mound 48 m high, grassed over with gas vents.
landmarks.why: The city's waste on the industrial island.
landmarks.look: A smooth green hill on flat land.
landmarks.memorable: The highest point on Corliss is made of rubbish.

landmarks.name: Shipyard Goliath Crane
landmarks.desc: A huge gantry crane straddling the main drydock.
landmarks.why: Lifts ship modules into the drydock.
landmarks.look: A giant red rectangle.
landmarks.memorable: The biggest machine in the islands.

landmarks.name: Refinery Flare
landmarks.desc: A tall flare stack burning off excess gas.
landmarks.why: Safety system of the refinery.
landmarks.look: An orange flame on a stick.
landmarks.memorable: The flame glowing on low clouds.

landmarks.name: Bellamy Grain Elevator
landmarks.desc: Concrete grain silos beside the railroad.
landmarks.why: Collects grain and peanuts for shipping by rail.
landmarks.look: Grey silos above flat land.
landmarks.memorable: The tallest thing in town.

landmarks.name: Peanut Water Tower
landmarks.desc: A water tower painted to look like a giant peanut.
landmarks.why: Town water tower in the peanut-growing county.
landmarks.look: A tan peanut on legs.
landmarks.memorable: Everyone photographs it.

landmarks.name: Calder Stadium
landmarks.desc: The football stadium on reclaimed land by the harbour.
landmarks.why: Large flat site near the highway.
landmarks.look: A bowl of lights.
landmarks.memorable: Light glowing over the harbour.

landmarks.name: Ledford Observation Tower and Tramway
landmarks.desc: A needle-like observation tower and an aerial tramway running up the side of Cove Mountain.
landmarks.why: Tourist town at the foot of the mountains.
landmarks.look: A needle and swinging cars.
landmarks.memorable: Tram cars against the mountain.

landmarks.name: Calder Harbor Light
landmarks.desc: A red cast-iron light at the tip of Calder Point.
landmarks.why: Marks the harbour entrance.
landmarks.look: A red tower on the seawall.
landmarks.memorable: Red against grey water.

landmarks.name: Graystone Head Light
landmarks.desc: A stubby white tower on the headland at the sound mouth.
landmarks.why: Marks the turn into Cassena Sound.
landmarks.look: White tower on dark rock.
landmarks.memorable: Ships passing close by.

landmarks.name: Cayo Lejos Light
landmarks.desc: A skeletal iron screwpile light on the outermost key.
landmarks.why: Marks the edge of the flats.
landmarks.look: An iron skeleton on a sandbar.
landmarks.memorable: The last structure before open water.

landmarks.name: Bellamy Solar Farm
landmarks.desc: Rows of solar panels covering an old cotton field.
landmarks.why: Flat, cleared farmland near transmission lines.
landmarks.look: Dark blue rectangles.
landmarks.memorable: Panels flashing in the sun from the air.

landmarks.name: Lake Whitlock Dam
landmarks.desc: A low stone dam with a waterfall spillway at the outlet of Lake Whitlock.
landmarks.why: Built to create the lake.
landmarks.look: Water sheeting over stone.
landmarks.memorable: The spillway falls under the road bridge.

landmarks.name: Bright Water Gullies
landmarks.desc: A maze of steep red, orange and white gullies up to 40 m deep, cut into the soft weathered rock of an abandoned field.
landmarks.why: Deeply weathered saprolite, once exposed, erodes very quickly.
landmarks.look: Bands of red, pink and cream in steep walls.
landmarks.near: Bright Water Road, Graystone Piedmont Pines.
landmarks.memorable: A painted canyon in the middle of farmland.

landmarks.name: Hollow Reach Power Span
landmarks.desc: A transmission line strung across the mouth of Hollow Reach between towers on either headland.
landmarks.why: Power to Graystone.
landmarks.look: Wires across the gorge mouth.
landmarks.memorable: Orange marker balls on the wires.

landmarks.name: Blind Tunnel
landmarks.desc: A stone-lined railroad tunnel portal at the foot of the Blue Wall that goes 400 m into the mountain and stops at a rock face.
landmarks.why: Graded and bored for a railroad up the escarpment that was never completed.
landmarks.look: A dark arch in a fern-covered cliff.
landmarks.memorable: Cold air flowing out of the dark.

landmarks.name: Bearpen Tunnel
landmarks.desc: A two-lane highway tunnel that carries the Gate Road under the spur of Bearpen Knob straight onto the Gate Bridge.
landmarks.why: The spur stands between the Hollow Reach rim and the bridge shelf.
landmarks.look: Portal lights and the bridge visible through the tunnel.
landmarks.memorable: Daylight and bridge at the end of the tunnel.

landmarks.name: Big Laurel Shay
landmarks.desc: The rusted frame and boiler of a geared logging locomotive lying on its side at the end of the old grade.
landmarks.why: Left where it stood when the logging railroad was pulled up.
landmarks.look: Orange rust and moss.
landmarks.memorable: A locomotive in the middle of a forest.

landmarks.name: The Sill Canal
landmarks.desc: A dead-straight canal dug eight kilometres into the swamp from Long Ridge, with a spoil bank along one side.
landmarks.why: Dug to drain the swamp; the swamp is perched and the canal never drained it.
landmarks.look: A ruler-straight line of water.
landmarks.memorable: Unnaturally straight in a world of curves.

landmarks.name: Cypress Tram Grade
landmarks.desc: A raised logging railroad grade running into the swamp, rails gone, with rotting crossties.
landmarks.why: Built to haul cypress logs out of the swamp.
landmarks.look: A straight raised path through cypress.
landmarks.memorable: Crossties sticking out of the mud.

landmarks.name: Turpentine Still Ruins
landmarks.desc: Brick firebox, copper fragments and rusted barrel hoops of a turpentine distillery.
landmarks.why: The longleaf forests were tapped for resin.
landmarks.look: Brick ruins among pines.
landmarks.memorable: Pines nearby still carry their catface scars.

landmarks.name: Phosphate Dragline
landmarks.desc: An abandoned walking dragline with its boom collapsed over a flooded pit.
landmarks.why: Left behind when phosphate mining stopped.
landmarks.look: A rusted machine the size of a house.
landmarks.memorable: A giant machine in the wilderness.

landmarks.name: Wickham Spring
landmarks.desc: A large spring where water boils up from a limestone vent into a pool of electric blue.
landmarks.why: The aquifer beneath the sand ridge discharges near the coast.
landmarks.look: Blue water over white sand.
landmarks.memorable: Water 22 °C all year round.

landmarks.name: Seacow Spring
landmarks.desc: A spring where manatees gather in winter.
landmarks.why: Warm spring water in cold months.
landmarks.look: Grey shapes in clear water.
landmarks.memorable: Manatees in winter.

landmarks.name: Kettle Shell Ring
landmarks.desc: A ring-shaped ridge of oyster shell 80 m across and four metres high, overgrown with cedar and palm.
landmarks.why: A shell midden on the edge of the marsh.
landmarks.look: A wooded ring in the marsh.
landmarks.memorable: A perfect ring seen from the air.

landmarks.name: Kettle Tabby Ruins
landmarks.desc: Roofless walls of tabby — oyster-shell concrete — standing in the woods.
landmarks.why: Buildings made from the local shell and lime.
landmarks.look: Grey shell-studded walls.
landmarks.memorable: Walls studded with shells.

landmarks.name: Rice Hope Trunk Gates
landmarks.desc: Wooden sluice gates in the dikes of old rice fields, still controlling the water.
landmarks.why: Rice was grown in diked fields flooded with fresh tidal water.
landmarks.look: Wooden boxes in earthen dikes.
landmarks.memorable: Old dikes still holding water.

landmarks.name: Beach Line Trestle Pilings
landmarks.desc: A line of timber pilings crossing the marsh where an excursion railroad once ran to the beach.
landmarks.why: Built to carry visitors to the ocean beach before the road.
landmarks.look: Black pilings marching across the marsh.
landmarks.memorable: Pilings in a straight line to nowhere.

landmarks.name: Boneyard Beach Trees
landmarks.desc: Bleached dead oaks and pines standing on an eroding beach.
landmarks.why: The shoreline is retreating into the forest.
landmarks.look: Silver trees in the surf.
landmarks.memorable: Sunrise through dead trees.

landmarks.name: Houses in the Surf
landmarks.desc: A row of beach houses standing on pilings in the surf zone after the beach eroded out from under them.
landmarks.why: Shoreline retreat on the barrier.
landmarks.look: Houses with waves breaking beneath.
landmarks.memorable: Waves washing under living rooms.

landmarks.name: Drowned Church Steeple
landmarks.desc: The stone steeple of a church on the old cove floor, which rises above the water only when the lake is drawn down in autumn.
landmarks.why: The cove was flooded by Calloway Lake.
landmarks.look: A steeple standing in mud flats.
landmarks.memorable: Only visible a few weeks a year.

landmarks.name: Ledford Gap Foundations
landmarks.desc: Stone foundations and a chimney base of a demolished hotel at the gap.
landmarks.why: A hotel stood at the pass when the road was built.
landmarks.look: Stone outlines in the grass.
landmarks.memorable: Steps leading up to nothing.

landmarks.name: Old Narrows Ferry Slip
landmarks.desc: A concrete ferry ramp and rotting dolphins at the old crossing, below the bridge.
landmarks.why: The ferry crossed here before the bridge.
landmarks.look: A ramp sliding into the water.
landmarks.memorable: Fishermen use it as a launch.

landmarks.name: Coldwater Covered Bridge
landmarks.desc: A red wooden covered bridge on an old road across the Coldwater River.
landmarks.why: Built where the old valley road crossed the river.
landmarks.look: A red barn-like bridge over clear water.
landmarks.memorable: The only covered bridge in the islands.

landmarks.name: Old Hominy Bridge
landmarks.desc: A collapsed steel truss bridge lying in Hominy Creek beside the concrete bridge that replaced it.
landmarks.why: Washed out in a flood and left in place.
landmarks.look: Twisted steel in the creek.
landmarks.memorable: Old and new bridges side by side.

landmarks.name: Serena Waterslide Ruins
landmarks.desc: Cracked concrete pools and the faded fibreglass tubes of an abandoned water park, overgrown with vines.
landmarks.why: A resort attraction built on the foreland and abandoned.
landmarks.look: Bright fibreglass tubes under kudzu.
landmarks.memorable: Faded colours in the jungle.

landmarks.name: Ocosta Shores
landmarks.desc: A grid of paved streets, street signs and fire hydrants with no houses, slowly being reclaimed by pines.
landmarks.why: A subdivision laid out and never built.
landmarks.look: Streets with nothing on them.
landmarks.memorable: Street signs in a pine forest.

landmarks.name: Bellamy Drive-In Screen
landmarks.desc: The tall screen tower of an abandoned drive-in theatre beside SR 9.
landmarks.why: Roadside business on the highway.
landmarks.look: A blank screen above a weedy field.
landmarks.memorable: A blank white screen at dusk.

landmarks.name: Merrin Shoals Boiler
landmarks.desc: The rusted boiler and ribs of a steamship exposed on the shoals at low tide.
landmarks.why: The shoals have trapped many ships.
landmarks.look: A rusty cylinder in the breakers.
landmarks.memorable: Breakers bursting over the boiler.

landmarks.name: Sunken Dredge
landmarks.desc: The hulk of a dredge resting on a sandbar off Corliss, its superstructure above water.
landmarks.why: Sank while working the ship channel.
landmarks.look: A rusty hulk with birds on it.
landmarks.memorable: Cormorants drying their wings on the wreck.

landmarks.name: Kestrel Concrete Tower
landmarks.desc: A windowless concrete observation tower standing alone in the dunes.
landmarks.why: Built on the dunes for its view of the sea.
landmarks.look: A grey cylinder with narrow slits.
landmarks.memorable: A strange tower in the dunes.

landmarks.name: Little Black Fish Camp
landmarks.desc: Stilt cabins, a bait shop and a boat ramp on the Little Black River.
landmarks.why: Access to the river for fishing.
landmarks.look: Cabins on stilts over black water.
landmarks.near: Little Black River, Sawpit Pass Bridge.
landmarks.memorable: Cane poles and screened porches.

landmarks.name: Trail Airboat Landing
landmarks.desc: An airboat ride landing beside the Trail with a gift shop.
landmarks.why: Access to the open prairies.
landmarks.look: Airboats with giant fans.
landmarks.memorable: The roar of airboat engines.

landmarks.name: Calloway Houseboats
landmarks.desc: Floating houses moored in rows in a cove of Calloway Lake.
landmarks.why: Sheltered cove near the marina.
landmarks.look: Floating houses on green water.
landmarks.memorable: A floating neighbourhood.

landmarks.name: Coldwater Tobacco Barns
landmarks.desc: Tall, narrow log barns with gaps between the boards for air-curing tobacco.
landmarks.why: Tobacco grown on the valley bottomland.
landmarks.look: Dark barns in pasture.
landmarks.memorable: Light shining through the gaps.

landmarks.name: Rich Mountain Chimney
landmarks.desc: A lone fieldstone chimney in a meadow where a house once stood.
landmarks.why: An old homestead clearing.
landmarks.look: A chimney in a meadow.
landmarks.memorable: Daffodils still bloom around it.

landmarks.name: Rich Creek Car Bank
landmarks.desc: A line of old car bodies laid along a creek bank to stop erosion.
landmarks.why: Used as riprap along the creek.
landmarks.look: Rusted car bodies in the creek bank.
landmarks.memorable: Old fenders in the water.

landmarks.name: Sugartree Sugar Shack
landmarks.desc: Stone foundations and rusted kettles of a maple sugar shack.
landmarks.why: Maples in the north-facing hollows.
landmarks.look: Kettles in the leaves.
landmarks.memorable: Kettles full of leaves.

landmarks.name: Gooseberry Boardwalk
landmarks.desc: A plank walkway across the bog pond.
landmarks.why: Protects the bog.
landmarks.look: Boards over moss.
landmarks.memorable: Sundews beside the boards.

landmarks.name: Hickory Falls Rock Shelter
landmarks.desc: An overhang behind the falls where the soft rock has eroded under the caprock.
landmarks.why: Soft shale beneath hard sandstone.
landmarks.look: A curtain of water across the entrance.
landmarks.memorable: Standing behind a waterfall.

landmarks.name: Blue Hole Rope Swing
landmarks.desc: A rope swing on a sycamore over the Blue Hole.
landmarks.why: The deep spring pool.
landmarks.look: Rope over blue water.
landmarks.memorable: Jumping into icy blue water.

landmarks.name: Stillhouse Branch Ruins
landmarks.desc: A rock-walled pit, copper scraps and barrel staves beside a hidden spring.
landmarks.why: A clean spring in a secluded hollow.
landmarks.look: Stone wall half buried in leaves.
landmarks.memorable: Copper turned green.

landmarks.name: Kudzu House
landmarks.desc: An abandoned farmhouse completely engulfed in kudzu vines.
landmarks.why: Abandoned fields on the Piedmont.
landmarks.look: A green shape of a house.
landmarks.memorable: Vines covering every surface.

landmarks.name: Bald Rock Pools
landmarks.desc: Round pools worn into the granite that fill with rainwater and tiny plants.
landmarks.why: Water dissolves the granite in small hollows.
landmarks.look: Pools reflecting the sky.
landmarks.memorable: Little mirrors on bare rock.

landmarks.name: Fallon Net Lofts
landmarks.desc: Tall narrow wooden lofts for drying nets on the quay.
landmarks.why: The fishing harbour.
landmarks.look: Black-tarred wooden buildings.
landmarks.memorable: The smell of tar and salt.

landmarks.name: Catface Pine
landmarks.desc: An old longleaf pine with a deep V-shaped scar from resin tapping.
landmarks.why: Pines tapped for turpentine.
landmarks.look: A face-like scar on the trunk.
landmarks.memorable: Old metal cups still nailed to it.

landmarks.name: Rice Hope Bottle Tree
landmarks.desc: A cedar tree with blue glass bottles on its branches beside a farmhouse.
landmarks.why: Yard decoration in the hamlet.
landmarks.look: Blue glass glinting in the sun.
landmarks.memorable: The bottles hum in the wind.

landmarks.name: Hollow Cypress
landmarks.desc: An ancient cypress with a hollow trunk you can paddle a canoe into.
landmarks.why: Too hollow for the loggers to bother with.
landmarks.look: A doorway in a giant tree.
landmarks.memorable: Paddling inside a tree.

landmarks.name: Freeze-Killed Mangroves
landmarks.desc: Grey skeletons of black mangroves killed by a hard freeze, with green regrowth among them.
landmarks.why: The northern limit of mangroves.
landmarks.look: Grey and green tangles.
landmarks.memorable: Life and death side by side.

landmarks.name: Lifesaving Station Slab
landmarks.desc: A concrete slab and rebar in the dunes.
landmarks.why: A station once stood on the open foreland.
landmarks.look: Concrete in the sand.
landmarks.memorable: Rebar poking out of dunes.

landmarks.name: Sheepshead Bait Shack
landmarks.desc: A weathered bait and tackle shack beside the inlet bridge.
landmarks.why: Inlet fishing.
landmarks.look: Hand-painted signs.
landmarks.memorable: The hand-painted fish menu.

landmarks.name: SR 1 Mile Zero
landmarks.desc: The zero-mile marker at the end of the Keys Highway.
landmarks.why: The southern end of the road.
landmarks.look: A green sign beside the water.
landmarks.memorable: The end of the road.

landmarks.name: Iron Cove Seeps
landmarks.desc: Orange iron-rich seeps staining the bluff and beach.
landmarks.why: Groundwater leaching iron from the Red Hills.
landmarks.look: Orange stains on red clay.
landmarks.memorable: Rust-coloured water.

landmarks.name: Sugarloaf Cemetery
landmarks.desc: An old hilltop cemetery under cedars beside the church.
landmarks.why: High ground for burial.
landmarks.look: Old headstones under cedars.
landmarks.memorable: Views over the farmland.

landmarks.name: Paper Mill Whistle
landmarks.desc: The steam whistle on the paper mill heard across the island at shift change.
landmarks.why: Mill shift signal.
landmarks.look: A brass whistle on a pipe.
landmarks.memorable: The whistle at 7 a.m.

landmarks.name: Gasholder Ring
landmarks.desc: The iron frame of a Victorian gasholder now enclosing a park.
landmarks.why: The old gasworks.
landmarks.look: An iron ring of columns.
landmarks.memorable: Lit at night.

landmarks.name: Mill Creek Outfall
landmarks.desc: A stone arch where the buried Mill Creek emerges into the harbour.
landmarks.why: The creek was culverted under the city.
landmarks.look: A dark stone arch at the waterline.
landmarks.memorable: A hidden creek reaching the sea.

landmarks.name: Cedar Point Light
landmarks.desc: A small iron skeleton light on the oyster bars off Cedar Point.
landmarks.why: Marks the channel to Cedar Shoals.
landmarks.look: An iron frame on the bars.
landmarks.memorable: Pelicans perched on top.

landmarks.name: Pelican Key Rookery
landmarks.desc: A small mangrove key covered in nesting pelicans and herons.
landmarks.why: Isolated key safe from predators.
landmarks.look: White birds covering green mangroves.
landmarks.memorable: The noise of the colony.

viewpoints.name: Ledford Dome Observation Tower
viewpoints.desc: A concrete spiral ramp to a circular deck above the spruce–fir on the highest summit.
viewpoints.why: Highest point in the islands; the trees would otherwise block the view.
viewpoints.look: Pale ramp curling above a black conifer canopy.
viewpoints.near: Ledford Dome Road, Ledford Spruce–Fir Forest.
viewpoints.memorable: Every island is visible on a clear day.

viewpoints.name: Ledford Gap Overlook
viewpoints.desc: A stone-walled parking area at the crest of the Gap Road where it meets the Parkway.
viewpoints.why: The pass is the low point of the crest and looks straight down the North Face.
viewpoints.look: Stone wall, interpretive sign, and a sheer drop toward the Narrows.
viewpoints.memorable: Clouds pouring through the gap from one side to the other.

viewpoints.name: Painted Bald
viewpoints.desc: Open summit meadow with views in every direction.
viewpoints.why: Treeless bald summit.
viewpoints.look: Grass and azalea foreground, blue ridges beyond.
viewpoints.memorable: Azaleas framing the whole western half of the archipelago.

viewpoints.name: Gooseberry Fire Tower
viewpoints.desc: A steel fire lookout cab on a grassy summit at the western end of the crest.
viewpoints.why: Built to watch the Coldwater Valley and the Tableland for smoke.
viewpoints.look: Steel stairs and a glass cab.
viewpoints.memorable: Sunset on the Tableland escarpment.

viewpoints.name: The Steeples
viewpoints.desc: A narrow rock perch between the twin slate spires.
viewpoints.why: Highest rock on the eastern crest.
viewpoints.look: Knife-edge rock with drops on both sides.
viewpoints.memorable: Looking down on Calloway Lake and across to Graystone.

viewpoints.name: Callahan Cliff Tops
viewpoints.desc: Bare slate ledges at the top of Mount Callahan's north face.
viewpoints.why: Cliffs on the steepest mountain face in the islands.
viewpoints.look: Grey ledges and a 1,800 m drop to the strait.
viewpoints.memorable: Ships in the Narrows look like toys.

viewpoints.name: Lookout Bluff
viewpoints.desc: The tip of the sandstone promontory at the edge of the Tableland.
viewpoints.why: Western edge of the plateau above the bay.
viewpoints.look: Flat rock prow with Serena Bay below.
viewpoints.memorable: Sunsets over Serena Bay and the Mirabel coast.

viewpoints.name: Hickory Falls Overlook
viewpoints.desc: A railed platform at the plateau rim beside the brink of Hickory Falls.
viewpoints.why: Where the plateau stream leaps off the escarpment.
viewpoints.look: The falls dropping into a green gorge, with the Coldwater Valley beyond.
viewpoints.memorable: The whole Coldwater Valley spread below.

viewpoints.name: Tableland Grade Pull-off
viewpoints.desc: A gravel pull-off on the switchbacks of the Tableland Road.
viewpoints.why: Halfway up the escarpment.
viewpoints.look: Road switchbacks below and the valley beyond.
viewpoints.memorable: Watching valley fog from above at dawn.

viewpoints.name: Calloway Dam Overlook
viewpoints.desc: A viewing terrace on the dam crest between the lake and the gorge.
viewpoints.why: The dam spans the narrowest point of the gorge.
viewpoints.look: Lake on one side, a 135 m drop on the other.
viewpoints.memorable: Spillway gates opening in a flood.

viewpoints.name: Thunderstone Overlook
viewpoints.desc: A Parkway pull-off facing the North Face spurs and the Narrows.
viewpoints.why: The Parkway crosses the crest just west of Ledford Gap.
viewpoints.look: Parallel spurs descending to the strait.
viewpoints.memorable: Spurs lined up like folded cloth.

viewpoints.name: Sawyer Gap Overlook
viewpoints.desc: Pull-off at the eastern end of the Parkway.
viewpoints.why: Low gap at the east end of the crest.
viewpoints.look: Upper Cove farms below, Graystone across Hollow Reach.
viewpoints.memorable: Farm fields deep in the mountains.

viewpoints.name: Hominy Bay Overlook
viewpoints.desc: A rest area on I-21 above Hominy Bay.
viewpoints.why: Where the interstate tops a foothill spur above the bay.
viewpoints.look: Wooded bay, sound and Bellamy beyond.
viewpoints.memorable: The first view of the sea for travellers from the mainland.

viewpoints.name: Narrows Bridge Crest
viewpoints.desc: The top of the Narrows Bridge cantilever, seen from a car.
viewpoints.why: Bridge over the strait at its narrowest point.
viewpoints.look: Steel truss and the North Face rising ahead.
viewpoints.memorable: The first sight of the islands from the mainland.

viewpoints.name: Whitlock Mountain Summit
viewpoints.desc: Granite summit ledges above the lake.
viewpoints.why: Highest point on Graystone.
viewpoints.look: Granite slabs and stunted spruce.
viewpoints.memorable: Lake below, sea on three sides.

viewpoints.name: Lantern Mountain
viewpoints.desc: Clearing beside the radar dome fence.
viewpoints.why: Summit cleared for the radar.
viewpoints.look: White dome above the clearing.
viewpoints.memorable: Ocean horizon to the east.

viewpoints.name: Pale Wall Rim
viewpoints.desc: The edge of the 230 m granite wall.
viewpoints.why: Top of the largest cliff in the islands.
viewpoints.look: Bare granite falling away to forest.
viewpoints.memorable: Standing above a sheer white wall.

viewpoints.name: Glassface Pull-off
viewpoints.desc: A switchback pull-off on the Whitlock Grade facing the dome.
viewpoints.why: The road passes close below the dome.
viewpoints.look: The shining rock face at eye level.
viewpoints.memorable: Ice-glazed rock in winter.

viewpoints.name: Grayback Summit
viewpoints.desc: The bare top of the granite monadnock.
viewpoints.why: Isolated dome rising above the plain.
viewpoints.look: Bare rock in all directions.
viewpoints.memorable: The Blue Wall on one side, the sound on the other.

viewpoints.name: Gate Bridge
viewpoints.desc: The suspension bridge deck 190 m above Hollow Reach.
viewpoints.why: The bridge crosses at the narrowest point of the gorge.
viewpoints.look: Gorge walls rising on both sides, water far below.
viewpoints.near: Gate Bridge, Veil Falls, Bearpen Tunnel.
viewpoints.memorable: Veil Falls visible up the gorge from the bridge.

viewpoints.name: Veil Falls Rim
viewpoints.desc: The lip of the cliff where Hollow Creek falls into Hollow Reach.
viewpoints.why: The creek leaps the gorge wall.
viewpoints.look: Water vanishing over the edge.
viewpoints.memorable: Spray rising back up the cliff.

viewpoints.name: Fallon Cliffs Pull-off
viewpoints.desc: A pull-off on the Coast Road at the cliff edge.
viewpoints.why: The road runs along the cliff top.
viewpoints.look: Ocean far below.
viewpoints.memorable: Gannets diving in the sea below.

viewpoints.name: Cape Fallon Light
viewpoints.desc: The gallery of the lighthouse on the north arm of Fallon Cove.
viewpoints.why: The headland guarding the harbour.
viewpoints.look: Harbour, cliffs and open sea.
viewpoints.memorable: Fishing boats returning at dusk.

viewpoints.name: Anvil Rock
viewpoints.desc: The flat top of the granite prow.
viewpoints.why: Projecting rock on the escarpment edge.
viewpoints.look: Drop on three sides.
viewpoints.memorable: The whole Piedmont strip and the sound below.

viewpoints.name: Ravenrock Ledges
viewpoints.desc: Dark gneiss ledges near the summit.
viewpoints.why: Cliff band near the top.
viewpoints.look: Dark rock and wheeling ravens.
viewpoints.memorable: Falcons stooping past the ledges.

viewpoints.name: Thunderhole Gorge Overlook
viewpoints.desc: A rock ledge above the gorge with a view of Thunderhole Falls.
viewpoints.why: Rim of the gorge where the river crosses the Blue Wall.
viewpoints.look: White falls in a green gorge.
viewpoints.memorable: The roar audible a kilometre away.

viewpoints.name: Heights Reservoir Park
viewpoints.desc: The promenade around the reservoir at the top of the Heights.
viewpoints.why: Highest ground in the city.
viewpoints.look: Skyline and harbour beyond the water.
viewpoints.memorable: The skyline reflected in the reservoir.

viewpoints.name: Calder Tower Observation Deck
viewpoints.desc: The observation floor at the top of the tallest building in the islands.
viewpoints.why: Downtown sits on the bluff at the river mouth.
viewpoints.look: Glass floor-to-ceiling windows.
viewpoints.memorable: Night view of three bridges lit up.

viewpoints.name: Tennalee River Bridge Crest
viewpoints.desc: The high point of the interstate bridge into the city.
viewpoints.why: The bridge spans the North Channel.
viewpoints.look: Downtown towers ahead.
viewpoints.memorable: The skyline appearing as you crest the bridge.

viewpoints.name: Landfill Hill
viewpoints.desc: The grassy top of the capped landfill.
viewpoints.why: Highest point on flat Corliss.
viewpoints.look: Cranes, stacks and ships.
viewpoints.memorable: Watching container ships berth.

viewpoints.name: Harbor Bridge
viewpoints.desc: The bridge between Calder and Corliss.
viewpoints.why: Crosses the Inner Harbor.
viewpoints.look: Port cranes and the city.
viewpoints.memorable: City on one side, industry on the other.

viewpoints.name: Iron Mountain
viewpoints.desc: A clearing on the ironstone cap.
viewpoints.why: Highest hill on Bellamy.
viewpoints.look: Farmland patchwork to the horizon.
viewpoints.memorable: Seeing the whole farm plain.

viewpoints.name: Long Bridge Hump
viewpoints.desc: The high navigation span of the Long Bridge.
viewpoints.why: Ships pass under the hump.
viewpoints.look: City ahead, sound on both sides.
viewpoints.memorable: The skyline rising out of the water.

viewpoints.name: Sound Bluffs
viewpoints.desc: The top of the red clay bluffs on the north shore.
viewpoints.why: Bluffs of the Red Hills at the sound.
viewpoints.look: Red cliffs and the mountains across the sound.
viewpoints.memorable: The whole Halcomb range across the water.

viewpoints.name: End of Mirabel Pier
viewpoints.desc: The T-head at the end of the fishing pier.
viewpoints.why: The pier extends past the surf.
viewpoints.look: Green water below, the strip behind.
viewpoints.memorable: Sunset with the condo towers glowing behind.

viewpoints.name: Cape Serena Light
viewpoints.desc: The gallery of the lighthouse on the foreland tip.
viewpoints.why: Lighthouse at the cape.
viewpoints.look: Beach ridges and dune lakes below.
viewpoints.near: Cape Serena Beach, Long Swale Lake.
viewpoints.memorable: The dune lakes in parallel rows.

viewpoints.name: Mirabel Sands Rooftop
viewpoints.desc: The rooftop of the tallest condominium tower.
viewpoints.why: The tallest building on the barrier.
viewpoints.look: Strip, sound and Bellamy farmland.
viewpoints.memorable: Both sides of the island at once.

viewpoints.name: Bay Street Bluff
viewpoints.desc: The bluff-top promenade along Haversham's waterfront.
viewpoints.why: The town sits on the highest bluff on the river.
viewpoints.look: Marsh, river and shrimp boats.
viewpoints.memorable: Golden marsh at sunrise.

viewpoints.name: Ambrose Inlet Bridge
viewpoints.desc: The high point of the inlet bridge.
viewpoints.why: High-rise span over the inlet.
viewpoints.look: Inlet shoals, the Banks running south.
viewpoints.memorable: The Banks stretching to the horizon.

viewpoints.name: Bonnet Marsh Tower
viewpoints.desc: A wooden observation tower in the marsh.
viewpoints.why: Built for birdwatchers.
viewpoints.look: Marsh to the horizon.
viewpoints.memorable: Herons and egrets at eye level.

viewpoints.name: Scrub Hill Fire Tower
viewpoints.desc: The steel fire tower on Wickham's highest point.
viewpoints.why: Fire lookout for the longleaf woods.
viewpoints.look: Forest in all directions.
viewpoints.memorable: Both coasts visible.

viewpoints.name: Fire Tower Hill
viewpoints.desc: An older fire tower at the south end of the ridge.
viewpoints.why: Second lookout on the ridge.
viewpoints.look: Longleaf savanna below.
viewpoints.memorable: Sunrise over the swamp island.

viewpoints.name: Cedar Point
viewpoints.desc: The tip of Cedar Point at the fish houses.
viewpoints.why: Southernmost point of Wickham.
viewpoints.look: Oyster bars and open water.
viewpoints.memorable: Sun setting over oyster bars.

viewpoints.name: Highpine Fire Tower
viewpoints.desc: Fire tower on Long Ridge.
viewpoints.why: Highest point on the island.
viewpoints.look: Swamp to the west, sound to the east.
viewpoints.memorable: The swamp as a green sea.

viewpoints.name: Big Water Tower
viewpoints.desc: A wooden observation tower at the end of a boardwalk.
viewpoints.why: Overlooks the open lake.
viewpoints.look: Lake and cypress.
viewpoints.memorable: Alligators below the tower.

viewpoints.name: Ossahatchee Skyway
viewpoints.desc: The elevated viaduct of the Trail across the swamp.
viewpoints.why: The road crosses the deepest part of the swamp on a viaduct.
viewpoints.look: Treetops on both sides.
viewpoints.memorable: Driving through the canopy.

viewpoints.name: Kestrel Hill
viewpoints.desc: The bare summit of the big dune.
viewpoints.why: Tallest dune on the Banks.
viewpoints.look: Ocean, sound and village.
viewpoints.memorable: Both ocean and sound at sunset.

viewpoints.name: Cape Merrin Lighthouse
viewpoints.desc: The gallery of the tallest lighthouse in the islands.
viewpoints.why: Lighthouse at the cape.
viewpoints.look: Breakers over the shoals and the wind farm.
viewpoints.memorable: Shoals breaking white kilometres offshore.

viewpoints.name: Sheepshead Inlet Bridge
viewpoints.desc: The crest of the inlet bridge.
viewpoints.why: High-rise span over the inlet.
viewpoints.look: Inlet and ocean.
viewpoints.memorable: Fishing boats running the inlet.

viewpoints.name: Sabal Bridges
viewpoints.desc: The low bridges to Sabal Key.
viewpoints.why: Bridges across the flats.
viewpoints.look: Clear water over seagrass.
viewpoints.memorable: The water colours of the flats.

beaches.name: Mirabel Beach
beaches.desc: The main resort beach: a wide, gently sloping strand of sugar-white quartz sand in front of condominium towers, with lifeguard stands and rows of umbrellas.
beaches.why: Quartz sand carried down from the crystalline highlands by the rivers and moved south along the coast by waves; the low-energy Gulf side keeps it fine and clean.
beaches.look: Squeaky white sand, emerald-green nearshore water turning deep blue past the sandbar.
beaches.near: Mirabel Pier, Pier District, Lake Mirabel, Beach Road.
beaches.memorable: Sunset straight out over Serena Bay behind the pier.

beaches.name: Pier Beach
beaches.desc: Beach on either side of the long concrete fishing pier, crowded with anglers and surfers in winter swells.
beaches.why: The pier interrupts longshore drift, so sand piles up on its north side.
beaches.look: Pier pilings marching into green water.
beaches.memorable: The pier lights at night.

beaches.name: Dunewood Beach
beaches.desc: A quieter beach backed by the island's highest dunes, crossed by long wooden walkovers.
beaches.why: Wider beach and higher dunes where the barrier swings slightly seaward.
beaches.look: White dunes with sea oats behind white sand.
beaches.memorable: Walkovers climbing 9 m dunes.

beaches.name: Seaholly Point
beaches.desc: A curving sand spit at the north tip of Mirabel where the pass into Cassena Sound runs fast at the change of tide.
beaches.why: Spit built north by longshore drift until the tidal current in the pass stops it.
beaches.look: Hooked spit with standing waves in the pass.
beaches.memorable: Dolphins feeding in the tidal rip.

beaches.name: Cape Serena Beach
beaches.desc: The point of the foreland, where the beach wraps around a sandy cape under a black-and-white light tower.
beaches.why: A cuspate foreland built where wave approaches from two directions meet.
beaches.look: Beach curving around a point under a lighthouse.
beaches.near: Cape Serena Light, Long Swale Lake.
beaches.memorable: Watching waves meet from two directions off the tip.

beaches.name: Dune Lakes Beach
beaches.desc: Wild beach on the foreland's west shore, where the dune lakes sometimes break through the beach to the bay.
beaches.why: Coastal dune lakes drain across the beach after heavy rain.
beaches.look: Tea-coloured outfall stream crossing white sand.
beaches.near: Cypress Dune Lake, Little Serena Lake.
beaches.memorable: A dark freshwater stream flowing across white sand into green water.

beaches.name: Old Station Beach
beaches.desc: Beach in front of a concrete slab and pilings where a lifesaving station once stood.
beaches.why: Exposed western shore of the foreland.
beaches.look: Concrete slab half-buried in sand.
beaches.memorable: Rusted rebar sticking out of the dunes.

beaches.name: Lagoon Beach
beaches.desc: A calm sound-side beach on Mirabel Sound with paddleboard rentals and shallow seagrass flats.
beaches.why: Sheltered lagoon shore with fine sand and almost no waves.
beaches.look: Glassy water and seagrass.
beaches.memorable: Water you can walk across at low tide.

beaches.name: Turtle Crawl Beach
beaches.desc: A dark-sky beach without streetlights, staked off in summer around sea turtle nests.
beaches.why: Wide, low beach between Mirabel Beach and Dunewood.
beaches.look: Orange nest stakes in the dunes.
beaches.memorable: Turtle tracks in the morning sand.

beaches.name: Causeway Beach
beaches.desc: A small beach of fill sand along the causeway approach on the Bellamy shore, popular for fishing.
beaches.why: Sand pumped in when the causeway was built.
beaches.look: Fishing rods lined along the causeway.
beaches.memorable: Families fishing at sunset.

beaches.name: Kestrel Beach
beaches.desc: A broad Atlantic beach of tan sand and crushed shell in front of the village and the big dune.
beaches.why: Wide beach where Kestrel Island is widest and sand supply is greatest.
beaches.look: Tan sand, steep surf, and the bare dune behind.
beaches.memorable: The dune towering over the beach.

beaches.name: Medano Beach
beaches.desc: Beach south of Kestrel where sand blows off the beach into the dune field.
beaches.why: Onshore winds strip the dry upper beach and feed the dunes.
beaches.look: Sand streaming off the beach in the wind.
beaches.memorable: Sand blowing like smoke across the road.

beaches.name: Cape Merrin Point
beaches.desc: The sharp tip of the cape, where waves from the north and south collide over the shoals.
beaches.why: Cape built where the barrier chain changes direction.
beaches.look: Crossing wave trains breaking over shoals.
beaches.memorable: Waves meeting head-on off the point.

beaches.name: Lighthouse Beach
beaches.desc: Surf beach below the Cape Merrin Light, with the remains of an earlier lighthouse foundation in the surf zone.
beaches.why: The cape shoreline has retreated past the old tower site.
beaches.look: Granite blocks in the breakers.
beaches.memorable: The old foundation appearing at low tide.

beaches.name: Shellbank Beach
beaches.desc: A beach of whole and broken shell beside Sheepshead Inlet.
beaches.why: The inlet's tidal currents sort out the coarse shell.
beaches.look: Crunchy beach of white and grey shell.
beaches.memorable: Collecting whelks and moon snails.

beaches.name: Pennick Beach
beaches.desc: A long, empty, south-facing beach reached only by ferry.
beaches.why: Pennick Island faces south toward the open Atlantic.
beaches.look: Kilometres of beach without a building.
beaches.memorable: Wild ponies grazing behind the dunes.

beaches.name: Rockfish Spit
beaches.desc: A shifting sand spit at Rockfish Inlet beside the ferry landing.
beaches.why: Inlet spits grow and wash away with every storm.
beaches.look: Sandbar that changes shape season to season.
beaches.memorable: The ferry channel moves every year.

beaches.name: Inlet Point
beaches.desc: The north tip of Kestrel Island beside Ambrose Inlet, under the inlet bridge.
beaches.why: Inlet shoals and a migrating spit.
beaches.look: Bridge piers rising out of shoals.
beaches.memorable: Fishing under the bridge lights at night.

beaches.name: Ambrose Beach
beaches.desc: The island's resort beach: a broad, hard-packed tan beach where the big Lowcountry tides leave hundreds of metres exposed at low water.
beaches.why: The large tidal range of the sound mouth makes very wide, flat beaches.
beaches.look: Wet sand reflecting the sky at low tide.
beaches.memorable: Riding bicycles on the beach at low tide.

beaches.name: Bonnet Inlet Beach
beaches.desc: A sandy spit along Bonnet Inlet with strong currents and sandbars.
beaches.why: Tidal inlet between the north and south beach islands.
beaches.look: Sandbars and swirling inlet water.
beaches.memorable: Sandbars that appear and disappear with the tide.

beaches.name: Boneyard Beach
beaches.desc: An eroding beach where the forest is falling into the sea: bleached, salt-killed oak and pine trunks stand and lie across the sand.
beaches.why: This part of the barrier is retreating landward, and the shoreline has moved through the forest.
beaches.look: Silver driftwood trees on the beach.
beaches.memorable: Sunrise silhouettes through dead trees.

beaches.name: South Ambrose Beach
beaches.desc: Quiet beach on the southern barrier near Ambrose Inlet.
beaches.why: Southern beach island.
beaches.look: Tan sand and low dunes.
beaches.memorable: Few footprints.

beaches.name: Oyster Point Shell Beach
beaches.desc: A beach of oyster shell on the north shore facing Corliss, with shrimp boats moored nearby.
beaches.why: Shell from oyster reefs washed up on the sound shore.
beaches.look: Grey shell beach with refinery lights across the water.
beaches.memorable: Industrial skyline across the water from a fishing village.

beaches.name: Kettle Shell Beach
beaches.desc: A small shell beach on Ketch Sound below Kettle Island.
beaches.why: Shell from oyster bars piled by waves.
beaches.look: Shell beach on a muddy shore.
beaches.memorable: The bridge high above the shell beach.

beaches.name: Hurricane Beach
beaches.desc: A wild beach on Wickham's south-east corner with uprooted trees and storm-overwash fans behind it.
beaches.why: The only part of Wickham exposed to Gulf waves; storms wash sand inland.
beaches.look: Sand fans spreading into the pines.
beaches.memorable: Storm-tossed trees half buried in sand.

beaches.name: Cedar Point Shell Beach
beaches.desc: A shell beach on the southern point beside the fish houses, with red cedars leaning over the sand.
beaches.why: Shell from the oyster reefs offshore.
beaches.look: Red cedars over a white shell beach.
beaches.memorable: Fish houses on stilts beside the beach.

beaches.name: Seacow Bar
beaches.desc: A sand and mud bar at the mouth of Seacow Spring Run where the clear spring water meets the bay.
beaches.why: Spring run sediment builds a bar in the bay.
beaches.look: Clear blue spring water meeting green bay water.
beaches.memorable: Manatees gathering in winter.

beaches.name: Landing Beach
beaches.desc: A narrow beach beside the Wickham ferry landing on Ketch Sound.
beaches.why: Small sandy shore on the north coast.
beaches.look: Ferry ramp beside a sandy beach.
beaches.memorable: The ferry nosing up to the ramp.

beaches.name: Turtle Bay Beach
beaches.desc: A shell beach at the head of Turtle Bay where the coastal highway runs close to the water.
beaches.why: Waves concentrate shell at the bay head.
beaches.look: Shell beach with mangroves on both sides.
beaches.memorable: A beach on the swamp coast.

beaches.name: Sabal Key Beach
beaches.desc: The outer beach of Sabal Key, coarse white shell and coral-like limestone fragments.
beaches.why: Outer shore of the key facing the Gulf.
beaches.look: White shell beach with palms.
beaches.memorable: Palms and shell, the most tropical beach in the islands.

beaches.name: Cayo Viento Beach
beaches.desc: A windswept beach on the outer key with stilt houses at its end.
beaches.why: Windward side of the key.
beaches.look: Stilt houses and shell beach.
beaches.memorable: Constant breeze.

beaches.name: Bonefish Bar
beaches.desc: A sandbar that connects Bonefish Key to shallow flats at low tide.
beaches.why: Tidal flats around the key.
beaches.look: Sand bar emerging from clear water.
beaches.memorable: Wading the flats looking for bonefish tails.

beaches.name: Cayo Lejos
beaches.desc: The most remote key, a ring of shell beach with a skeletal light tower.
beaches.why: Outermost key on the edge of the flats.
beaches.look: A tiny island with a light tower.
beaches.memorable: The edge of the archipelago.

beaches.name: Turtlegrass Key Beach
beaches.desc: A small beach backed by black mangrove.
beaches.why: Outer shore of the westernmost key.
beaches.look: Shell beach against dark mangroves.
beaches.memorable: Rarely visited.

beaches.name: Hominy Bay Beach
beaches.desc: A crescent of coarse quartz sand at the head of Hominy Bay with a public swimming area.
beaches.why: Hominy Creek delivers granite-derived sand to the bay head.
beaches.look: Coarse golden sand in a wooded bay.
beaches.memorable: Mountains rising directly behind a beach.

beaches.name: Shady Point Beach
beaches.desc: A beach on the southern point of Halcomb's south-west lobe, looking across the sound to Bellamy.
beaches.why: The point catches sand moving along the south shore.
beaches.look: Sand point with mountains behind.
beaches.memorable: View of the whole Cassena Sound.

beaches.name: Piney Cove
beaches.desc: A tiny cobble cove under the Tableland Bluffs where Piney Creek falls from the cliff top straight onto the beach.
beaches.why: The creek has notched the bluffs but not cut a valley, so it leaps the cliff.
beaches.look: A ribbon of waterfall onto rounded cobbles.
beaches.memorable: A waterfall pouring onto a beach.

beaches.name: Pigeonroost Beach
beaches.desc: A cobble beach at the foot of the Gap Road where Pigeonroost Creek meets the Narrows.
beaches.why: Creek delta of rounded mountain cobbles.
beaches.look: Grey cobbles with the mainland across the strait.
beaches.memorable: The North Face rising straight up behind.

beaches.name: Calloway Swim Beach
beaches.desc: A small trucked-in sand beach on Calloway Lake with a roped swimming area.
beaches.why: Built at the most sheltered shore near the village.
beaches.look: Sand beach and floating dock on a mountain lake.
beaches.memorable: Jumping off the dock into cold green water.

beaches.name: Fallon Cove Beach
beaches.desc: A cobble and gravel beach at the head of Fallon Cove where boats are hauled out.
beaches.why: River gravel from the Fallon River trapped in the cove.
beaches.look: Boats on a grey gravel beach under cliffs.
beaches.memorable: Waves rattling the cobbles.

beaches.name: Veil Falls Shingle
beaches.desc: A tiny shingle beach at the foot of Veil Falls in Hollow Reach, reachable only by boat.
beaches.why: Talus and creek gravel at the foot of the gorge wall.
beaches.look: A waterfall falling 130 m onto a pocket beach.
beaches.memorable: Spray drifting across the water.

beaches.name: Head Cove Beach
beaches.desc: A pocket beach tucked behind Graystone Head.
beaches.why: Sheltered from swell by the headland.
beaches.look: Small cove beach under rocks.
beaches.memorable: Ships passing close outside.

beaches.name: Stillhouse Beach
beaches.desc: A cobble beach at the foot of Stillhouse Branch on the north shore.
beaches.why: Creek mouth on the north coast.
beaches.look: Cobbles with the mainland in view.
beaches.memorable: The quietest beach on Graystone.

beaches.name: Cutstone Bay Beach
beaches.desc: A coarse granite-sand beach in the shallow bay west of Graystone town.
beaches.why: Granite weathers into coarse quartz and feldspar grit.
beaches.look: Pinkish coarse sand.
beaches.memorable: Pink sand from the granite.

beaches.name: Westside Park Beach
beaches.desc: An urban beach and seawall promenade in Westside Park.
beaches.why: Sand placed along the sheltered west shore.
beaches.look: City beach with towers behind.
beaches.memorable: Swimming with the skyline behind you.

beaches.name: South Shore Beach
beaches.desc: A narrow beach below the South Shore seawall facing Saint Ambrose.
beaches.why: Sand accumulates against the seawall.
beaches.look: Narrow strip of sand below a wall.
beaches.memorable: Watching ships pass the Long Bridge hump.

beaches.name: Spoil Island Beach
beaches.desc: A beach of dredged sand on the east tip of Corliss beside the shipyard.
beaches.why: Built from channel dredging spoil.
beaches.look: Grey sand under gantry cranes.
beaches.memorable: Watching ships arrive at the port.

beaches.name: Sound Bluffs Beach
beaches.desc: A beach below red clay bluffs on Bellamy's north shore, littered with ironstone pebbles.
beaches.why: Waves undercut the soft Red Hills sediments and leave the hard ironstone.
beaches.look: Red cliffs above a pale beach.
beaches.memorable: Red bluffs glowing at sunset.

beaches.name: Old Bridge Beach
beaches.desc: A muddy sand beach on the Ashwood River where the piers of the old swing bridge now carry a fishing walkway.
beaches.why: Tidal river shore beside the crossing.
beaches.look: Old concrete piers stepping into brown water beside the new high-rise bridge.
beaches.near: Ashwood River Bridge, Ashwood Swing Bridge.
beaches.memorable: Old and new bridges side by side.

beaches.name: Iron Cove Beach
beaches.desc: A cove beach with dark iron-stained sand.
beaches.why: Iron minerals eroded from the Red Hills.
beaches.look: Rust-streaked sand.
beaches.memorable: Black and rust sand patterns.

lakes.name: Calloway Lake
lakes.where: Tennalee Cove, central Halcomb, behind Calloway Dam
lakes.desc: A long, branching reservoir that drowned the lower Tennalee Cove and the hollows around it. Arms of deep green water reach up every tributary valley; floating houseboats are moored in the sheltered coves.
lakes.why: A 135 m concrete dam in the narrow quartzite gorge below the cove stores the Tennalee for power and flood control.
lakes.look: Fjord-like, many-fingered outline under steep wooded slopes; a pale "bathtub ring" of bare clay shows when the water is drawn down in autumn.
lakes.near: Calloway Dam, Calloway village and marina, Cove Mountain, Huckleberry Knob, Upper Cove.
lakes.memorable: In late autumn the drawdown exposes old roadbeds, stone walls and chimneys from the drowned valley.

lakes.name: Lake Hominy
lakes.where: Hominy Creek valley north of Hominy
lakes.desc: A small reservoir with a grassy earth dam and a concrete spillway, surrounded by forest with no development on its shores.
lakes.why: Dams the narrow lower valley of Hominy Creek to supply Ledford and Hominy.
lakes.look: A narrow ribbon of water in a wooded valley.
lakes.near: Hominy, Chestnut Knob, Sugartree Knob, I-21.
lakes.memorable: The stepped spillway roars white after storms.

lakes.name: Hickory Lake
lakes.where: Hickory Tableland, on Hickory Creek above Hickory Falls
lakes.desc: A tea-coloured lake on the flat plateau top, edged by sandstone ledges and stunted pine.
lakes.why: A low dam on Hickory Creek holds water on the impermeable sandstone caprock.
lakes.look: Dark water reflecting pale rock.
lakes.near: Hickory Falls, Hickory Knob, Hickory Flat.
lakes.memorable: Its outflow plunges off the escarpment a few hundred metres downstream.

lakes.name: Sinking Pond
lakes.desc: A shallow pond that fills in winter and drains through its floor every summer, leaving a meadow of sedges.
lakes.why: Collapse into limestone beneath the thin sandstone cap.
lakes.look: Some years a lake, some years a meadow.
lakes.memorable: Its water disappears underground every summer.

lakes.name: The Blue Hole
lakes.where: Coldwater Valley floor north of Coldwater
lakes.desc: A small, almost perfectly round spring pool of startlingly clear blue water, 22 m deep, overhung by sycamores.
lakes.why: Groundwater from the limestone valley rises through a solution shaft.
lakes.look: Electric blue water in a green pasture.
lakes.near: Coldwater River, Coldwater, the Old Valley Road.
lakes.memorable: You can see the bottom from the edge despite the depth.

lakes.name: Coldwater Quarry Lake
lakes.where: East side of the Coldwater Valley near the Narrows
lakes.desc: A water-filled limestone quarry with sheer grey walls and turquoise water.
lakes.why: An abandoned section of the limestone quarry filled with groundwater.
lakes.look: Turquoise water in a grey rock box.
lakes.near: Coldwater Limestone Quarry, I-21, Narrows Landing.
lakes.memorable: Its colour looks unreal next to the green valley.

lakes.name: Gooseberry Pond
lakes.desc: A tiny sphagnum bog pond surrounded by sedges, cranberry and stunted red maple.
lakes.why: A shallow hollow on the crest with impermeable soil.
lakes.look: Black water in a ring of bright moss.
lakes.near: Gooseberry Bald fire tower, the Parkway.
lakes.memorable: A bog at 1,300 m on a southern island.

lakes.name: Big Laurel Millpond
lakes.where: Big Laurel Creek above Big Laurel village
lakes.desc: A small pond behind a dry-laid stone dam with the foundations of a mill at its foot.
lakes.why: An old dam built to power a sawmill on the only gentle reach of the creek.
lakes.look: Still water above a stone wall.
lakes.near: Big Laurel, Big Laurel Logging Grade.
lakes.memorable: The mill's iron water wheel lies rusting below the dam.

lakes.name: Lake Whitlock
lakes.where: Whitlock Basin on the Graystone highlands
lakes.desc: A clear mountain lake held by a low stone dam on the upper Thunderhole, with summer houses, boathouses and a stone chapel along its shore.
lakes.why: A dam at the outlet of the highland basin created the lake for the summer colony.
lakes.look: Still water reflecting Whitlock Mountain's granite face.
lakes.near: Whitlock village, Whitlock Mountain, the Highlands Road.
lakes.memorable: Mirror reflections of granite and fall colour at dawn.

lakes.name: Bright Water Lake
lakes.where: Headwaters of the Bright Water River
lakes.desc: A small lake in a hollow on the plateau, ringed by rhododendron.
lakes.why: Water ponded behind a granite sill at the head of the Bright Water.
lakes.look: Dark water edged by pink rhododendron in June.
lakes.memorable: The outflow pours over the granite sill into the gorge.

lakes.name: Fallon Reservoir
lakes.desc: A narrow reservoir in a steep valley with a concrete arch dam.
lakes.why: Water supply for Fallon, built where the valley narrows between granite walls.
lakes.look: A thin curved dam between cliffs.
lakes.memorable: The curved dam is barely 20 m wide at its crest.

lakes.name: Cutstone Quarry Hole
lakes.where: Cutstone Mountain west of Graystone town
lakes.desc: A deep, emerald-green flooded pit with terraced granite benches, rusted derrick footings and cables.
lakes.why: The lowest bench of the granite quarry filled with water after pumping stopped.
lakes.look: Emerald water in a grey stepped bowl.
lakes.near: Cutstone, Cutstone Quarry, Blue Wall Incline.
lakes.memorable: Old derrick masts still stand on the rim.

lakes.name: Heights Reservoir
lakes.desc: A rectangular stone-lined reservoir on the summit of the Heights, surrounded by a jogging path and a wrought-iron fence.
lakes.why: Built on the highest ground in the city to give gravity pressure to the water mains.
lakes.look: A rectangle of water ringed by city lights.
lakes.near: Calder Heights broadcast tower, the Heights district.
lakes.memorable: The skyline reflected in still water at dusk.

lakes.name: Lake Ellery
lakes.desc: A curving park lake with stone bridges, a boathouse and islands of bald cypress.
lakes.why: A former tidal creek mouth on the west shore dammed and landscaped into a park.
lakes.look: Cypress knees in still water with towers behind.
lakes.memorable: The city's only swamp, planted with cypress a century ago.

lakes.name: Corliss Cooling Pond
lakes.where: East Corliss beside the generating station
lakes.desc: A long rectangular pond of warm water that steams on cold mornings.
lakes.why: Cooling water for the generating station's condensers.
lakes.look: A steaming pond under smokestacks.
lakes.near: Corliss Generating Station, Corliss Landfill Hill.
lakes.memorable: Winter mornings the pond is wrapped in its own fog.

lakes.name: Lake Ocosta
lakes.desc: A narrow, winding reservoir in the Ocosta valley with an earth dam and a water-treatment plant.
lakes.why: The upper Ocosta was dammed to supply Bellamy and Bellamy Bluffs.
lakes.look: A narrow ribbon of water between red-clay bluffs.
lakes.near: Sugarloaf Hill, Bellamy Solar Farm, Red Hills Road.
lakes.memorable: Red clay bluffs reflected in brown water.

lakes.name: Clearwater Bay
lakes.desc: The largest of the oval bay lakes: shallow, clear, with a white sand bottom and a sand rim on its south-east shore, surrounded by bay forest and cypress.
lakes.why: One of the elliptical depressions that dot the coastal plain, all aligned north-west to south-east.
lakes.look: A perfect ellipse from the air, white sand under tea-coloured water.
lakes.near: Ocosta River, Ocosta Nuclear Station, Moon Lake.
lakes.memorable: Wading out a hundred metres and still knee-deep on white sand.

lakes.name: Tar Kiln Bay
lakes.desc: A dark-water bay lake ringed by pocosin, with remains of a tar kiln mound on its sand rim.
lakes.why: Carolina bay depression in the flatwoods.
lakes.look: A dark oval in a ring of dense green shrubs.
lakes.memorable: The blackened kiln mound on the rim.

lakes.name: Brown's Bay
lakes.desc: A small bay lake with cypress fringing its shallow north-west end.
lakes.why: Carolina bay depression.
lakes.look: Oval lake with a fringe of cypress.
lakes.memorable: Its cypress fringe glows rust-red in November.

lakes.name: Little Bay
lakes.desc: A small, almost-filled bay with open water only in its centre.
lakes.why: A bay being slowly filled by peat.
lakes.look: Open water inside a ring of marsh.
lakes.memorable: You can see the whole cycle of a bay filling in.

lakes.name: Sand Bay
lakes.desc: A shallow bay with a high white sand rim used as a swimming beach.
lakes.why: Carolina bay with a well-developed sand rim.
lakes.look: White sand rim on one side.
lakes.memorable: A beach in the middle of farmland.

lakes.name: Moon Lake
lakes.desc: A crescent oxbow of the Ocosta, choked with water lilies and cypress.
lakes.why: An abandoned meander loop cut off by the river.
lakes.look: A perfect crescent.
lakes.memorable: Seen from the air, a crescent moon in the forest.

lakes.name: Ox Lake
lakes.desc: A narrow oxbow with standing dead cypress.
lakes.why: Abandoned meander of the Ocosta.
lakes.look: Grey snags in a crescent of water.
lakes.memorable: Herons nest in the dead cypress.

lakes.name: The Chalk Pits
lakes.desc: A string of flooded kaolin pits with milky turquoise water and chalk-white banks.
