lakes.why: Kaolin clay mined where the old upland sands contain thick clay lenses.
lakes.look: Bright white banks around chalky blue water.
lakes.near: Harlow, Iron Mountain, Red Hills Road.
lakes.memorable: White cliffs in red-clay country.

lakes.name: Cypress Dune Lake
lakes.where: Mirabel foreland near the Gulf beach
lakes.desc: A long, narrow freshwater lake in a swale between beach ridges, ringed by cypress and slash pine.
lakes.why: Fresh water ponded in the swales of the beach-ridge plain; storms occasionally open an outfall to the bay.
lakes.look: Dark fresh water a few steps from white sand.
lakes.memorable: Fresh and salt water within sight of each other.

lakes.name: Little Serena Lake
lakes.desc: A narrow swale lake bordered by marsh and pine.
lakes.why: Swale between beach ridges.
lakes.look: Long sliver of water between pine ridges.
lakes.memorable: Mirror-flat water at dawn.

lakes.name: Long Swale Lake
lakes.desc: The longest swale lake, curving parallel to the coast.
lakes.why: Follows an old shoreline.
lakes.look: A curving ribbon of water.
lakes.memorable: It traces the shape of an ancient beach.

lakes.name: Oyster Lake
lakes.desc: A small brackish swale lake with oyster shell on its bottom.
lakes.why: A swale lake that occasionally connects to the lagoon.
lakes.look: Grey-green water with shell beaches.
lakes.memorable: Oyster shells in a pond.

lakes.name: Lake Mirabel
lakes.where: Golf course in central Mirabel Beach
lakes.desc: An artificial lake with fountains surrounded by golf greens and condominiums.
lakes.why: Excavated for stormwater and fill during resort construction.
lakes.look: Fountains and putting greens.
lakes.memorable: Alligators sunning beside the 7th green.

lakes.name: Blue Sink
lakes.where: West flank of the Sandhill Ridge
lakes.desc: A round, deep sinkhole lake of clear blue water in a ring of longleaf pine.
lakes.why: Collapse of the limestone beneath the sand ridge into an underground cave system.
lakes.look: A circle of deep blue in pale sand.
lakes.near: Scrub Hill, Turpentine Tram grade, Wickham Spring.
lakes.memorable: Cave divers enter the aquifer through its floor.

lakes.name: Punchbowl Sink
lakes.desc: A steep-walled sinkhole with ferns and dripping limestone walls around a small pool 30 m below the rim.
lakes.why: Recent collapse into the aquifer.
lakes.look: A green funnel in the scrub.
lakes.near: Scrub Hill fire tower, Ridge Road.
lakes.memorable: Ten degrees cooler at the bottom than at the rim.

lakes.name: Round Lake
lakes.where: East flank of the Sandhill Ridge
lakes.desc: A circular lake with a white sand shoreline and longleaf to the water's edge.
lakes.why: Old sinkhole partly filled with sand.
lakes.look: A round lake with white beaches.
lakes.memorable: Perfectly round from the fire tower.

lakes.name: Deep Lake
lakes.desc: A small, very deep lake with steep sides and dark water.
lakes.why: Deep solution sinkhole.
lakes.look: Dark water in a steep basin.
lakes.memorable: Its water is cold even in August.

lakes.name: Sand Lake
lakes.desc: A broad, shallow lake with wide white sand beaches.
lakes.why: Coalesced shallow sinkholes on the ridge flank.
lakes.look: White sand and pale water.
lakes.memorable: The widest beach on Wickham is on a lake.

lakes.name: Little Sink
lakes.where: South end of the Sandhill Ridge
lakes.desc: A tiny sinkhole pond in the scrub.
lakes.why: Small collapse sinkhole.
lakes.look: A pocket of water in dense scrub.
lakes.near: Fire Tower Hill, Cedar Shoals road.
lakes.memorable: Easy to walk past without seeing.

lakes.name: Gator Pond
lakes.desc: A shallow marshy pond with lily pads and a resident population of alligators.
lakes.why: Wet depression in the poorly drained flatwoods.
lakes.look: Lily pads and eyes in the water.
lakes.memorable: The alligators are the reason for the name.

lakes.name: The Phosphate Pits
lakes.desc: A row of long, straight-sided water-filled trenches with spoil ridges between them.
lakes.why: Abandoned phosphate mining in the limestone.
lakes.look: Parallel strips of water from the air.
lakes.memorable: Geometric scars in the wilderness.

lakes.name: Big Water
lakes.where: Central Ossahatchee swamp south of the Trail
lakes.desc: A long, narrow lake of tea-coloured water lined with cypress and hanging moss.
lakes.why: A deep channel in the peat where water moves slowly west.
lakes.look: A dark ribbon through cypress.
lakes.near: Ossahatchee Skyway, Big Water observation tower.
lakes.memorable: The water is so dark it reflects like a mirror.

lakes.name: Cowhouse Lake
lakes.desc: An open lake surrounded by wet prairie.
lakes.why: A low point in the peat surface.
lakes.look: Open water in a sea of grass.
lakes.memorable: One of the few open horizons in the swamp.

lakes.name: Sill Lake
lakes.where: Eastern swamp near the Sill Canal
lakes.desc: A small lake at the end of an abandoned straight canal.
lakes.why: Ponded where the canal spoil blocked drainage.
lakes.look: A lake at the end of a ruler-straight canal.
lakes.memorable: The canal points straight at it.

lakes.name: Dinner Pond
lakes.desc: A small pond in the cypress with a fishing platform.
lakes.why: Gator hole kept open in the peat.
lakes.look: A clearing of water in cypress.
lakes.memorable: A favourite fishing spot.

lakes.name: Honey Lake
lakes.desc: A lake surrounded by tupelo trees.
lakes.why: Wet hollow at the swamp margin.
lakes.look: Tupelo trees standing in water.
lakes.memorable: Bee hives on platforms along its shore.

lakes.name: Black Lake
lakes.desc: The darkest lake in the swamp.
lakes.why: Deep peat-stained water.
lakes.look: Ink-black water.
lakes.memorable: Visibility a few centimetres.

lakes.name: Long Ridge Pond
lakes.desc: A small, clear sinkhole pond among longleaf pines.
lakes.why: Collapse through the dune ridge into limestone.
lakes.look: Clear water in white sand.
lakes.memorable: Clear water on the edge of a black-water swamp.

lakes.name: Borrow Pit Lake
lakes.desc: A long, straight pond beside the highway.
lakes.why: Dug to provide fill for the road causeway.
lakes.look: A straight ribbon of water beside the road.
lakes.memorable: Alligators lining the bank beside traffic.

lakes.name: The Rice Reserve
lakes.where: Central Saint Ambrose near Rice Hope
lakes.desc: A freshwater impoundment held by earthen dikes with wooden trunk gates.
lakes.why: Built to store fresh water for flooding rice fields.
lakes.look: Square-edged water with dikes.
lakes.memorable: Wooden trunk gates still control the water.

lakes.name: Cypress Pond
lakes.desc: A small cypress pond in the live-oak forest.
lakes.why: Fresh water ponded in a hollow of the sea-island core.
lakes.look: Cypress in still water.
lakes.memorable: Wood storks wade its edges.

lakes.name: Heron Pond
lakes.desc: A diked brackish pond used by wading birds.
lakes.why: Old impoundment on the marsh edge.
lakes.look: Bird-filled shallows.
lakes.memorable: Hundreds of herons at dusk.

lakes.name: Merrin Woods Pond
lakes.desc: A small freshwater pond in the maritime forest, among dune ridges.
lakes.why: Fresh water perched in the dune swales of the cape.
lakes.look: Fresh water under live oaks.
lakes.memorable: A freshwater pond on a sand island.

lakes.name: Sabal Salt Pond
lakes.desc: A shallow, hypersaline pond that turns pink in summer.
lakes.why: Evaporation pond on the low centre of the key.
lakes.look: Pink water.
lakes.memorable: Its summer colour.

forests.name: Ledford Spruce–Fir Forest
forests.desc: The archipelago's only boreal forest: dense red spruce and Fraser fir above about 1,850 m, floored with moss, wood sorrel and blowdowns, with grey dead fir on the exposed shoulders.
forests.why: The summits are cold enough — mean annual temperature near 7 °C — to support a relict northern forest left from colder climates.
forests.look: Almost black conifer canopy, often in cloud; the trees drip even on dry days.
forests.near: Ledford Dome, Mount Sawyer, Coldspring Knob, the Parkway.
forests.memorable: Walking out of a southern hardwood forest into what smells like Canada.

forests.name: Balsam Crest Northern Hardwoods
forests.desc: A belt of yellow birch, American beech and yellow buckeye along the high crest, twisted by ice storms, with beech gaps of short, gnarled trees in the saddles.
forests.why: The cool band between the oak forests and the spruce–fir.
forests.look: Gold in mid-October, earlier than the valleys.
forests.near: Painted Bald, Stormhead Mountain, the Parkway.
forests.memorable: Moss-draped birch trunks in fog.

forests.name: Callahan Old-Growth Coves
forests.desc: Uncut cove forest on the North Face: tulip poplars and buckeyes two metres across, a jungle of rhododendron along the streams, and a ground layer of trillium and fern.
forests.why: The North Face was too steep for the logging railroads; deep, moist coves facing north grow the largest trees.
forests.look: Enormous straight grey trunks rising into a closed canopy.
forests.near: Mount Callahan, Callahan Branch, Big Laurel Creek.
forests.memorable: Trees so wide three people cannot reach around them.

forests.name: Big Laurel Second Growth
forests.desc: Even-aged second-growth forest over the old logging grade, with rusting cable, rail spikes and a collapsed trestle in the hollows.
forests.why: Logged by railroad a century ago, now grown back as dense young forest.
forests.look: Straight, crowded trees all the same size.
forests.near: Big Laurel Logging Grade, Big Laurel Top, Big Laurel Millpond.
forests.memorable: Iron artefacts of the logging era scattered in the leaf litter.

forests.name: Hemlock Ghost Forest
forests.desc: A stand of dead eastern hemlocks, grey and needle-less, standing over a thicket of rhododendron and young hardwoods.
forests.why: Cool, north-facing coves where hemlock once dominated.
forests.look: A grey patch on the green mountainside.
forests.near: Hemlock Knob, Big Laurel Creek headwaters.
forests.memorable: Silent grey trunks above green undergrowth.

forests.name: Pigeonroost Laurel Hells
forests.desc: Impenetrable thickets of rhododendron and mountain laurel along the steep Pigeonroost valley.
forests.why: Steep, moist, acidic slopes where heaths outcompete trees.
forests.look: Dense evergreen shrub cover, pink in June.
forests.near: Pigeonroost Creek, the Gap Road, Blackstrap Knob.
forests.memorable: The Gap Road switchbacks tunnel through blooming laurel.

forests.name: Brushy Mountain Oak–Pine
forests.desc: Dry chestnut oak, scarlet oak and pitch pine forest with the grey snags of an old fire.
forests.why: South-facing slopes and thin soils that dry out every summer.
forests.look: Open, sunny woods with blueberry underneath.
forests.near: Brushy Mountain, Chestnut Knob, Lake Hominy.
forests.memorable: The smell of hot pine needles.

forests.name: Hickory Tableland Woods
forests.desc: Chestnut oak, hickory and Virginia pine on the flat plateau, with sandstone outcrops and blueberry thickets.
forests.why: Thin, sandy plateau soils over sandstone.
forests.look: Flat, open forest on a level horizon.
forests.near: Hickory Knob, Hickory Lake, Cane Creek.
forests.memorable: Perfectly flat forest ending at a 400 m cliff.

forests.name: Hickory Gorge Ravines
forests.desc: Shaded ravines below the plateau rim, with waterfalls, hemlock and moss-covered sandstone boulders.
forests.why: Plateau streams have cut deep, cool gorges into the escarpment.
forests.look: Green twilight and the sound of falling water.
forests.near: Hickory Falls, Cane Creek, Coldwater Valley.
forests.memorable: Cool air pouring out of the gorges on hot days.

forests.name: Dogwood Mountain Forest
forests.desc: Chestnut oak and hickory with a dense understory of flowering dogwood.
forests.why: Dry east-facing slopes above Hollow Reach.
forests.look: White dogwood bloom in April.
forests.near: Dogwood Mountain, the Gate Road, Upper Cove.
forests.memorable: Spring bloom visible from the Gate Bridge.

forests.name: Cove Mountain Poplars
forests.desc: Big tulip poplar and basswood in the deep coves on the lake side of Cove Mountain.
forests.why: Moist, sheltered coves facing the lake.
forests.look: Tall straight trunks and yellow autumn colour.
forests.near: Cove Mountain, Calloway Lake, Little River.
forests.memorable: The yellow coves reflected in the lake in October.

forests.name: Coldwater Valley Woodlots
forests.desc: Scattered woodlots of oak and red cedar on limestone knobs between the valley pastures.
forests.why: The rocky knobs are too thin-soiled to plough.
forests.look: Dark cedar clumps dotting green pasture.
forests.near: Coldwater, Blue Hole, Old Valley Road.
forests.memorable: Cedar knobs like islands in the valley floor.

forests.name: Hogback Woods
forests.desc: Pine and oak forest on the narrow quartzite ridge beside the gorge.
forests.why: Hard, nutrient-poor quartzite.
forests.look: Thin forest over white rock ledges.
forests.near: The Hogback, Calloway Dam, Tennalee Falls.
forests.memorable: White quartzite glinting through the trees.

forests.name: Blue Wall Rainforest
forests.desc: A temperate rainforest on the escarpment face: hemlock, rhododendron, ferns, mosses and liverworts on every surface, with waterfalls in every ravine.
forests.why: Moist sea air rises up the escarpment and drops over 2,500 mm of rain a year — the wettest place in the islands.
forests.look: Saturated green; the escarpment seems to steam after rain.
forests.near: Glassface Dome, Thunderhole Gorge, the Whitlock Grade.
forests.memorable: Moss so thick the rocks look upholstered.

forests.name: Thunderhole Gorge Forest
forests.desc: Old forest on the walls of the gorge, too steep ever to have been cut.
forests.why: Inaccessible gorge walls.
forests.look: Dense forest clinging to steep walls.
forests.near: Thunderhole Falls, Thunderhole River.
forests.memorable: The roar of the falls through the trees.

forests.name: Whitlock Highland Forest
forests.desc: Northern red oak, birch and maple across the highland plateau, with rhododendron in the hollows.
forests.why: Cool, wet highland climate at 1,000–1,500 m.
forests.look: Brilliant autumn colour across a rolling plateau.
forests.near: Whitlock, Lake Whitlock, Bald Rock.
forests.memorable: October colour that draws crowds from the city.

forests.name: Lantern Mountain Red Spruce
forests.desc: A small relict stand of red spruce on the cold north side of Lantern Mountain.
forests.why: A cold, cloud-bathed north slope at the limit of spruce's range.
forests.look: Dark spires among the hardwoods.
forests.near: Lantern Mountain radar dome.
forests.memorable: The southernmost spruce in the islands.

forests.name: Fallon Cliff-Top Woods
forests.desc: Stunted oaks and pines on the cliff tops, sheared flat and leaning landward by salt wind.
forests.why: Constant onshore wind and salt spray.
forests.look: Tree tops combed smooth and flat.
forests.near: Fallon Cliffs, Coast Road, Cape Fallon.
forests.memorable: Trees shaped like the wind.

forests.name: Grayback Granite Glades
forests.desc: Outcrop vegetation on and around Grayback: mosses, lichens, red-stemmed succulents in the pools, and a fringe of red cedar.
forests.why: Bare granite with thin soil islands.
forests.look: Red and green carpets on grey rock in spring.
forests.near: Grayback Mountain, Bright Water Road.
forests.memorable: Tiny red plants in rain pools on bare rock.

forests.name: Wolfpen Laurel Slopes
forests.desc: Dense laurel and rhododendron under oak on the slopes above Hollow Reach.
forests.why: Steep, acidic, moist slopes.
forests.look: Pink bloom above the gorge in June.
forests.near: Wolfpen Mountain, Gate Shelf, Blue Wall Road.
forests.memorable: Laurel blooming above the Gate Bridge.

forests.name: Bright Water Coves
forests.desc: Rich cove forest along the Bright Water gorge with waterfalls and pools.
forests.why: Sheltered gorge below the escarpment.
forests.look: Green gorge with white water.
forests.near: Bright Water River, Hornet Spire.
forests.memorable: Swimming holes under cascades.

forests.name: Graystone Piedmont Pines
forests.desc: Loblolly pine and oak on the rolling hills below the Blue Wall, with old farm terraces and gullies.
forests.why: Old fields on red clay abandoned and grown back in pine.
forests.look: Pine forest with eroded red gullies.
forests.near: Grayback, Bright Water, Graystone.
forests.memorable: Stone walls and terraces in the woods.

forests.name: Frostcap Heath
forests.desc: A heath bald of rhododendron and laurel on the frost-exposed summit.
forests.why: Wind and ice keep trees from establishing.
forests.look: Low, dense, dark shrubs on the summit.
forests.near: Frostcap, Bright Water Lake.
forests.memorable: Rime-coated rhododendron in winter.

forests.name: Ocosta River Bottoms
forests.desc: Floodplain forest of water oak, sweetgum, sycamore and cypress along the Ocosta, flooded each winter.
forests.why: The river's floodplain floods regularly and stays fertile.
forests.look: High-water marks on tree trunks.
forests.near: Ocosta River, Moon Lake, Ox Lake.
forests.memorable: Canoeing through flooded forest in February.

forests.name: Red Hills Pine Woods
forests.desc: Open longleaf and shortleaf pine woods with wiregrass, burned every couple of years.
forests.why: Well-drained sandy hills with regular fire.
forests.look: Tall pines spaced widely over grass.
forests.near: Iron Mountain, Sugarloaf Hill, Red Hills Road.
forests.memorable: Smoke from spring burns drifting over the farms.

forests.name: Bay Rim Pocosins
forests.desc: Dense evergreen shrub bogs of bay, titi and gallberry around the Carolina bays.
forests.why: Saturated, peaty soils around the bays.
forests.look: Dark, glossy evergreen thickets.
forests.near: Clearwater Bay, Tar Kiln Bay, Brown's Bay.
forests.memorable: Impassable shrubs a few steps from open farmland.

forests.name: Sweetwater Swamp
forests.desc: A cypress and gum swamp along Sweetwater Creek.
forests.why: Low, wet creek bottom near the coast.
forests.look: Cypress knees in black water.
forests.near: Sweetwater, Mirabel Sound.
forests.memorable: Mist in the cypress at dawn.

forests.name: Bellamy Pine Plantations
forests.desc: Rows of slash and loblolly pine planted for pulpwood, at every stage from fresh clearcut to mature stand.
forests.why: Poorly drained flatwoods are better for pine than for crops.
forests.look: Straight rows of identical trees.
forests.near: Dunmore, Bellamy Highway, Wickham Ferry.
forests.memorable: Rows that flicker past the car window.

forests.name: Chalybeate Ravines
forests.desc: Steep ravines in the Red Hills with beech, magnolia and iron-stained springs.
forests.why: Streams cutting into the soft upland sediments.
forests.look: Deep wooded ravines with orange seeps.
forests.near: Harlow, Chalk Pits.
forests.memorable: Rusty spring water staining the creek beds.

forests.name: Ambrose Maritime Forest
forests.desc: Live oak, cabbage palm and magnolia hung with Spanish moss, with old dirt roads shaded into tunnels.
forests.why: The old sea-island core, high and dry enough for hardwood forest.
forests.look: Spanish moss and twisted live oaks.
forests.near: Rice Hope, Cypress Pond, Haversham Regional Airport.
forests.memorable: Driving through tunnels of moss-hung oaks.

forests.name: Kettle Island Pines
forests.desc: Slash pine and palmetto on the southern sea-island core.
forests.why: Sandy, slightly lower ground than the main core.
forests.look: Pines over palmetto.
forests.near: Kettle, Kettle Shell Beach.
forests.memorable: Palmetto rattling in the wind.

forests.name: Edgewater Hammocks
forests.desc: Live oak hammocks on Edgewater Island surrounded by marsh.
forests.why: Islands of higher ground in the marsh.
forests.look: Dark tree islands in tan marsh.
forests.near: Edgewater, Heron Pond.
forests.memorable: Tree islands floating on golden marsh.

forests.name: Bonnet Marsh Hammocks
forests.desc: Small palm and cedar hammocks scattered through the Bonnet River marsh.
forests.why: Old shell middens and sand ridges in the marsh.
forests.look: Palm islands in the marsh.
forests.near: Bonnet River, Banks Highway.
forests.memorable: Palms silhouetted against marsh sunsets.

forests.name: Haversham Oak Avenue
forests.desc: An avenue of huge live oaks leading from the town to an old house site.
forests.why: Planted along an old road on the bluff.
forests.look: Arched oak branches over a dirt road.
forests.near: Haversham, Haversham River.
forests.memorable: The arching canopy over the avenue.

forests.name: Sandhill Longleaf Savanna
forests.desc: Old-growth longleaf pine over wiregrass, with turkey oaks and gopher tortoise burrows, burned every few years.
forests.why: Deep, dry sand on the relict dune ridge; regular fire.
forests.look: Widely spaced pines over golden grass.
forests.near: Scrub Hill, Blue Sink, Ridge Road.
forests.memorable: Old pines with turpentine catface scars.

forests.name: Scrub Hill Scrub
forests.desc: Sand pine, scrub oaks and rosemary on bare white sand at the top of the ridge.
forests.why: The driest, sandiest soil on the island.
forests.look: Low, grey-green scrub on white sand.
forests.near: Scrub Hill, Punchbowl Sink.
forests.memorable: A desert landscape in a wet climate.

forests.name: Springs Hammock
forests.desc: Hardwood hammock of live oak, magnolia, cabbage palm and southern red cedar around the springs and spring runs.
forests.why: Moist, limestone-rich soils near the springs.
forests.look: Dense, shady forest beside crystal-clear water.
forests.near: Wickham Spring, Seacow Spring, Wickham.
forests.memorable: Cool shade beside 22 °C spring water.

forests.name: Sawpit Cypress Strand
forests.desc: A long strand of cypress along the Sawpit River.
forests.why: Drainage line through the eastern flatwoods.
forests.look: Tall cypress along a creek.
forests.near: Sawpit River, Gator Pond.
forests.memorable: Cypress knees standing in clear water.

forests.name: Cedar Point Hammock
forests.desc: Southern red cedar and live oak on the shell ridge at Cedar Point.
forests.why: Shell ridges on the coast support hardwood hammock.
forests.look: Wind-twisted red cedars.
forests.near: Cedar Shoals, Cedar Point Shell Beach.
forests.memorable: Twisted cedars over white shell.

forests.name: Big Water Cypress
forests.desc: Tall bald cypress hung with Spanish moss lining the Big Water channel, with ancient trees spared by loggers because they were hollow.
forests.why: The deepest, permanently flooded part of the swamp.
forests.look: Grey trunks and moss reflected in black water.
forests.near: Big Water, Ossahatchee Skyway, Big Water tower.
forests.memorable: Paddling among cypress older than the islands' towns.

forests.name: Long Ridge Longleaf
forests.desc: Longleaf pine along the dry crest of Long Ridge.
forests.why: Sandy relict barrier ridge, the only dry high ground on the island.
forests.look: A line of tall pines above the swamp.
forests.near: Highpine Knoll, Coastal Highway, Tarrow Landing.
forests.memorable: A highway of dry pines beside a sea of swamp.

forests.name: Sill Bay Forest
forests.desc: Dense bay forest of loblolly bay, sweetbay and red bay on deep peat near the Sill Canal.
forests.why: Peat that rarely floods deeply but never dries.
forests.look: Glossy evergreen canopy.
forests.near: Sill Lake, the Sill Canal.
forests.memorable: The sweet smell of bay leaves.

forests.name: Tolar Cutover
forests.desc: Second-growth pine on a large pine island logged for the sawmill at Tolar, with sawdust piles and mill foundations.
forests.why: A large island of sandy ground in the swamp.
forests.look: Young pines among old mill ruins.
forests.near: Tolar, the Trail.
forests.memorable: Mounds of old sawdust still smoking after lightning strikes.

forests.name: Little Black Gum Swamp
forests.desc: Black gum and cypress along the Little Black River.
forests.why: The river's floodplain through the western swamp.
forests.look: Swollen gum trunks in dark water.
forests.near: Little Black River, Black Lake, Dinner Pond.
forests.memorable: Red gum leaves on black water in autumn.

forests.name: Sabal Coast Mangroves
forests.desc: Black mangrove thickets mixed with salt marsh along the south coast, with patches of grey dead mangroves killed by rare hard freezes.
forests.why: The northern limit of mangroves: only the warmest, most sheltered shore supports them.
forests.look: Dark green thickets with grey freeze-killed patches.
forests.near: Sabal Landing, Sabal Bridges, Turtle Bay.
forests.memorable: Grey skeletons of freeze-killed mangroves among living ones.

forests.name: Foreland Ridge Forest
forests.desc: Slash pine and live oak on the beach ridges of the Mirabel foreland, with marshy swales between.
forests.why: Old beach ridges stable long enough to grow forest.
forests.look: Parallel ridges of pine and marsh.
forests.near: Dune lakes, Cape Serena Light.
forests.memorable: Walking across rows of old shorelines.

forests.name: Serena Scrub
forests.desc: Sand pine and rosemary scrub on old dunes south of Dunewood.
forests.why: Old dunes too dry for other trees.
forests.look: Grey-green scrub on white dunes.
forests.near: Dunewood, Beach Road.
forests.memorable: Rosemary scent on the dunes.

forests.name: Merrin Woods
forests.desc: Maritime forest on the widest part of the cape: live oak, loblolly pine and dogwood among old dune ridges.
forests.why: The only part of the Banks wide enough to shelter a forest from salt spray.
forests.look: A dark green patch on a sand island.
forests.near: Merrin, Merrin Woods Pond, Cape Merrin Light.
forests.memorable: A forest in the middle of the ocean.

forests.name: Kestrel Thickets
forests.desc: Salt-pruned thickets of wax myrtle and yaupon behind the dunes.
forests.why: Salt spray keeps woody plants low.
forests.look: Dense low shrubs trimmed flat by the wind.
forests.near: Kestrel Hill, Kestrel village.
forests.memorable: Shrubs sculpted by the wind.

forests.name: Westside Park Woods
forests.desc: The city's largest park: oak woods, lawns and the cypress lake on Calder's west shore.
forests.why: Low, wet ground on the west shore left as parkland.
forests.look: A green block against the grid.
forests.near: Lake Ellery, Westside Park Beach.
forests.memorable: Old oaks in the middle of the city.

mountains.name: Ledford Dome
mountains.where: Centre of the Balsam Crest, 1.7 km east of Ledford Gap
mountains.desc: The highest point in the archipelago: a broad, rounded summit wrapped in dark red spruce and Fraser fir, crowned by a concrete observation tower reached by a spiral ramp. Grey trunks of dead fir stand among the living trees on the windward south-west shoulder.
mountains.why: The crest is the core of the old crystalline massif, where resistant gneiss has outlasted the surrounding schists; at 2,047 m it is high enough for a relict boreal forest even at 30° N.
mountains.look: Black-green cone of conifers above a paler band of hardwoods, often capped in cloud while the valleys are clear; the tower's white ramp is visible from Calder on clear winter mornings.
mountains.near: Ledford Gap, the Parkway, Ledford Dome Road parking lot, Coldspring Knob, the Pigeonroost and Ledford Prong headwaters.
mountains.memorable: From the tower the whole archipelago lies below — the North Face dropping to the Narrows, Calloway Lake, the city on its island, and the flat southern islands fading into haze.

mountains.name: Mount Sawyer
mountains.where: Balsam Crest, 3.5 km east of Ledford Dome
mountains.desc: A long, double-topped summit ridge under spruce–fir with grassy openings where old fir blowdowns never regrew. A rough trail follows the crest between its two tops.
mountains.why: Second culmination of the same resistant gneiss band that forms Ledford Dome; the crest is continuous here because no stream has cut back through it.
mountains.look: A level skyline of dark conifers seen from the south as a wall above Calloway Lake.
mountains.near: Mount Callahan spur, Hemlock Knob, Callahan Branch headwaters, the Parkway.
mountains.memorable: Its flat top makes the crest look like a rampart running east from Ledford Dome.

mountains.name: Mount Callahan
mountains.where: North Face, on the spur north of Mount Sawyer
mountains.desc: A massive, free-standing mountain that rises almost 2,000 m directly from the Narrows in less than five kilometres. Grey cliffs of slate and phyllite break out on its north-west face below a summit of spruce, fir and heath.
mountains.why: A thrust slice of harder metasediment pushed north over the softer rocks; the Narrows strait has cut away its base, leaving the steepest relief in the islands.
mountains.look: Seen from the mainland bridge it looks like a separate peak standing in front of the crest, with pale cliffs catching the late sun.
mountains.near: Callahan Branch, Big Laurel Creek, the Narrows Road, Pigeonroost.
mountains.memorable: The mountain fills the windshield the whole way across the Narrows Bridge.

mountains.name: Coldspring Knob
mountains.where: Balsam Crest, west of Ledford Gap
mountains.desc: A sharp knob with a cluster of steel relay towers and their equipment huts on a cleared summit, surrounded by northern hardwoods and spruce.
mountains.why: Part of the main crest; its summit was cleared because it has the clearest radio path to both Calder and the mainland.
mountains.look: Red aircraft lights blink on its towers at night above Ledford.
mountains.near: Ledford Gap, Thunderstone spur, Brushy Mountain, the Parkway.
mountains.memorable: The towers are the first thing travellers see from the Gap Road switchbacks below.

mountains.name: Hemlock Knob
mountains.where: Balsam Crest, between Mount Sawyer and The Steeples
mountains.desc: A rounded summit whose north slope holds a stand of dead and dying hemlocks — grey, needle-less trunks above a dense rhododendron understory.
mountains.why: Cool, north-facing slope where hemlock once dominated the coves below the spruce zone.
mountains.look: A pale grey patch on an otherwise dark green flank, visible from the North Face.
mountains.near: Big Laurel Creek headwaters, Huckleberry Knob, the Parkway.
mountains.memorable: The grey "ghost forest" on its shoulder is unlike any other slope on the island.

mountains.name: Painted Bald
mountains.where: Western Balsam Crest, above the Hominy headwaters
mountains.desc: A treeless summit meadow of oatgrass and blueberry ringed by stunted beech, ablaze with flame azalea in June and red blueberry leaves in October.
mountains.why: Exposed summit swept by winter winds and ice, where an open meadow has persisted for generations.
mountains.look: A tawny bald patch on the dark crest, unmistakable from Hominy Bay.
mountains.near: Sugartree Knob, Stormhead Mountain, the Parkway overlooks.
mountains.memorable: The only place on the crest where you can see in every direction while standing in grass.

mountains.name: Stormhead Mountain
mountains.where: Western Balsam Crest, where the Rich Mountain spur branches north
mountains.desc: A steep-sided peak with a craggy summit of mica schist, oak and rhododendron on its flanks, and windswept beech on top.
mountains.why: Junction of two ridges, so it stands slightly above both; storms off Serena Bay hit it first.
mountains.look: Usually the first peak to disappear into afternoon thunderheads.
mountains.near: Rich Mountain, Painted Bald, Gooseberry Bald, the Parkway.
mountains.memorable: Lightning-scarred snags on the summit and a reputation for the first storm of the day.

mountains.name: The Steeples
mountains.where: Eastern Balsam Crest, above Big Laurel Top
mountains.desc: Twin spires of steeply tilted slate rising above heath and stunted pine, joined by a narrow rocky saddle. Loose plates of rock litter the trail to the top.
mountains.why: Near-vertical beds of slate weather into knife-edges where the crest narrows.
mountains.look: Two sharp points like church spires on the skyline, visible from Riverside and the Tennalee River Bridge.
mountains.near: Hemlock Knob, Sawyer Gap, Big Laurel spur, the Parkway.
mountains.memorable: The only jagged summit on a crest of rounded domes.

mountains.name: Blackstrap Knob
mountains.where: North Face, on the spur west of Mount Callahan
mountains.desc: A steep knob of dark slate with a scar of fresh rock where a landslide stripped its west face to bedrock.
mountains.why: Thin soils over steeply dipping slate fail during the heavy remnant-hurricane rains that hit the North Face.
mountains.look: A long pale streak down a dark green slope.
mountains.near: Pigeonroost Creek, the Gap Road switchbacks, Mount Callahan.
mountains.memorable: The landslide scar is visible from the Narrows Road and from boats in the strait.

mountains.name: Thunderstone Mountain
mountains.where: North Face, spur between Rich Creek and Pigeonroost Creek
mountains.desc: A broad, steep mountain with a summit of heath and table mountain pine and a north face of mossy boulder fields.
mountains.why: One of the parallel spurs that radiate north from the crest toward the Narrows.
mountains.look: A tall, dark pyramid above Narrows Landing.
mountains.near: Rich Creek, Pigeonroost Creek, the Narrows Road.
mountains.memorable: Its boulder field rings hollowly under foot and holds snow weeks after the summit melts.

mountains.name: Gooseberry Bald
mountains.where: Western end of the Balsam Crest above Shady Gap
mountains.desc: A grassy summit with a steel fire lookout tower, a small sphagnum pond, and the first Parkway pull-off after the climb from Shady Gap.
mountains.why: The crest drops away westward here, giving an unobstructed view over the Coldwater Valley and the Hickory Tableland.
mountains.look: Fire tower silhouetted on a bare summit.
mountains.near: Gooseberry Pond, Sheepback Bald, Pinnacle Knob, the Parkway.
mountains.memorable: Sunset from the tower sets the whole Tableland escarpment glowing orange.

mountains.name: Big Laurel Top
mountains.where: North Face spur above Big Laurel village
mountains.desc: A heavily forested summit cut by an abandoned logging railroad grade that zigzags up its western flank.
mountains.why: Spur between Big Laurel Creek and the Narrows Branch; the only North Face slope gentle enough for a logging railroad.
mountains.look: Visible switchback scars under second-growth forest.
mountains.near: Big Laurel Logging Grade, Big Laurel Millpond, the Narrows.
mountains.memorable: The old grade benches read like contour lines drawn on the mountain.

mountains.name: Huckleberry Knob
mountains.where: South of Hemlock Knob, above the north arm of Calloway Lake
mountains.desc: A heath-covered knob of huckleberry and mountain laurel above oak forest, with ledges looking straight down onto the lake.
mountains.why: Short spur off the crest whose thin soils support heath rather than forest.
mountains.look: A rust-coloured knob in autumn above blue water.
mountains.near: Calloway Lake, Upper Cove, Tennalee Cove.
mountains.memorable: The best place to see the full branching outline of Calloway Lake.

mountains.name: Bearpen Knob
mountains.where: Eastern end of the crest, above Hollow Reach
mountains.desc: The last high point before the crest drops into Hollow Reach: a rocky knob with a sheer eastern drop and the Bearpen Tunnel beneath its southern shoulder.
mountains.why: The crest ends abruptly where the drowned gorge of Hollow Reach cuts through the massif.
mountains.look: A dark headwall rising behind the western tower of the Gate Bridge.
mountains.near: Sawyer Gap, the Gate Shelf, Hollow Reach, Dogwood Mountain.
mountains.memorable: From the Gate Bridge it looks like the island's wall ends in a fist.

mountains.name: Sheepback Bald
mountains.where: North-west spur from Gooseberry Bald
mountains.desc: A long, smooth, grassy ridge grazed by cattle in summer, with a few wind-bent hawthorns.
mountains.why: Rounded ridge of deeply weathered schist that holds deep soil and has stayed open pasture.
mountains.look: A pale green whaleback above the Coldwater Valley.
mountains.near: Copperhead Knob, the Coldwater Valley, the Old Valley Road.
mountains.memorable: The only high summit where cattle graze, their bells audible from the valley.

mountains.name: Cove Mountain
mountains.where: Spur dividing the Ledford Prong valley from Tennalee Cove
mountains.desc: A heavily wooded mountain with a fire road to a small cleared summit and steep coves holding old-growth tulip poplar.
mountains.why: Spur between two drainages that funnel moist air into its coves.
mountains.look: Dark forested mass between the Ledford strip and the lake.
mountains.near: Calloway Lake, Ledford, Little River, Calloway Dam Road.
mountains.memorable: Its coves hold the largest trees on the island's south side.

mountains.name: Brushy Mountain
mountains.where: South spur between Hominy Creek and Ledford Prong
mountains.desc: A dry, oak-and-pine mountain on the sunny side of the crest, with an old burn scar of standing dead pine.
mountains.why: South-facing slopes dry out quickly and burn in drought years.
mountains.look: Lighter, patchier green than the coves around it.
mountains.near: Chestnut Knob, Lake Hominy, the Gap Road.
mountains.memorable: Grey snags of the old burn bristle along its crest.

mountains.name: Rich Mountain
mountains.where: North-west spur off Stormhead Mountain
mountains.desc: A rounded mountain of deep, dark soil with rich cove forests and an abandoned homestead clearing near the top.
mountains.why: Weathered mafic rock produces unusually fertile soils.
mountains.look: Exceptionally lush, dark canopy; a lone stone chimney in a meadow.
mountains.near: Rich Creek, Thunderstone, the Narrows Road.
mountains.memorable: The chimney standing alone in its clearing.

mountains.name: Sugartree Knob
mountains.where: South spur from Painted Bald above Hominy
mountains.desc: A knob covered in sugar maple, with an old sugar-shack foundation and rusted kettles in a hollow below the summit.
mountains.why: North-facing hollows on the spur hold maples at a lower elevation than usual.
mountains.look: Blazes orange in October, a week before the surrounding oaks.
mountains.near: Sugartree Branch, Hominy, Painted Bald.
mountains.memorable: The earliest and brightest autumn colour visible from I-21.

mountains.name: Dogwood Mountain
mountains.where: East of Tennalee Cove above the Hollow Reach rim
mountains.desc: A broad, wooded mountain whose understorey of flowering dogwood turns the slopes white in April.
mountains.why: Spur that separates the cove from the steep Hollow Reach shore.
mountains.look: White spring bloom under bare canopy, visible from the Gate Road.
mountains.near: Dogwood Creek, Upper Cove, the Gate Road, Hollow Reach.
mountains.memorable: For two weeks each spring the mountain looks dusted with snow.

mountains.name: Pinnacle Knob
mountains.where: West end of the crest above Shady Gap
mountains.desc: A small, steep knob with a rock outcrop at its point and the Parkway curling around its flank.
mountains.why: Last high ground before the crest drops into Shady Gap.
mountains.look: A pointed hill above the interstate corridor.
mountains.near: Shady Gap, I-21, the Parkway, Coldwater Valley.
mountains.memorable: Marks the start of the climb onto the crest.

mountains.name: Chestnut Knob
mountains.where: Foothills between Hominy and Ledford
mountains.desc: A foothill knob with sprouting American chestnut stumps among oaks, and a cell tower on its summit.
mountains.why: Dry, acidic ridge soils once dominated by chestnut.
mountains.look: Low wooded hill with a single lattice tower.
mountains.near: Lake Hominy, I-21, Ledford.
mountains.memorable: Chestnut sprouts still push up from century-old root crowns.

mountains.name: Copperhead Knob
mountains.where: East wall of the Coldwater Valley, north of Coldwater
mountains.desc: A rocky foothill knob with sunny limestone ledges and a small abandoned copper prospect pit.
mountains.why: Edge of the crystalline massif where it meets the limestone of the valley.
mountains.look: Grey ledges above green pasture.
mountains.near: Coldwater, Sheepback Bald, the Old Valley Road.
mountains.memorable: Overlooks the whole valley floor and the plateau escarpment opposite.

mountains.name: The Hogback
mountains.where: Low ridge east of the Lower Tennalee Gorge, above Tennalee Falls
mountains.desc: A narrow, steep-sided ridge of hard quartzite that the Tennalee cuts through just below Calloway Dam.
mountains.why: Resistant quartzite forms a long hogback that holds up the gorge where the dam was built.
mountains.look: A sharp, wooded ridgeline above the falls town.
mountains.near: Calloway Dam, Tennalee Falls, the Lower Tennalee Gorge.
mountains.memorable: Its quartzite ledges frame both ends of the dam.

mountains.name: Hickory Knob
mountains.where: Northern Hickory Tableland
mountains.desc: The highest point on the sandstone plateau: a low, rocky rise of conglomerate in a forest of chestnut oak and pitch pine.
mountains.why: Remnant of a thicker caprock layer on the tilted plateau surface.
mountains.look: A slight swell in the otherwise level tableland horizon.
mountains.near: Hickory Lake, Cane Creek gorge, the Tableland Bluffs.
mountains.memorable: Pebble-studded conglomerate boulders that look like poured concrete.

mountains.name: Lookout Bluff
mountains.where: West edge of the Hickory Tableland above Serena Bay
mountains.desc: A sandstone promontory at the plateau rim, dropping 400 m to the bay in a single sweep of cliffs and wooded talus.
mountains.why: The plateau is being cut back by the sea, leaving headlands where the caprock is thickest.
mountains.look: A flat-topped prow of pale rock above the water.
mountains.near: Piney Cove, Hickory Tableland Airport, the Tableland Road.
mountains.memorable: Sunsets over Serena Bay with the whole Mirabel shoreline in view.

mountains.name: Whitlock Mountain
mountains.where: Whitlock Range, north of Lake Whitlock
mountains.desc: The highest summit on Graystone: a granite-cored mountain with a bare south face of exfoliating rock sheets and a summit forest of red oak, rhododendron and scattered red spruce.
mountains.why: A large granite pluton that weathers into domes and sheets rather than ridges.
mountains.look: A pale, curved rock face above the village and lake.
mountains.near: Whitlock, Lake Whitlock, Hawkbill Knob, Lantern Mountain.
mountains.memorable: Its south face turns pink at sunrise above the still lake.

mountains.name: Lantern Mountain
mountains.where: Whitlock Range, east of Whitlock Mountain
mountains.desc: A broad summit topped by a white FAA radar dome and a lattice tower with red and white lights.
mountains.why: Second-highest point on the Graystone highlands with an unobstructed view out to sea.
mountains.look: A white golf ball on the skyline by day, a red pulse by night.
mountains.near: Bald Rock, Frostcap, Highlands Road, Ravenfork.
mountains.memorable: Visible from almost every island; the radar dome is a navigation mark for small planes.

mountains.name: Frostcap
mountains.where: Eastern Whitlock Range
mountains.desc: A cold, north-facing summit where rime ice coats the trees through much of the winter.
mountains.why: Exposed to winter northwest winds coming off the Narrows.
mountains.look: Silver-white crown of frosted trees on clear winter mornings.
mountains.near: Bright Water Lake, Ravenrock, the north-shore cliffs.
mountains.memorable: The only summit that looks snowy without snow.

mountains.name: Sassafras Knob
mountains.where: Western Graystone highlands
mountains.desc: A wooded knob with a rock overlook facing south over the Blue Wall and the Piedmont strip.
mountains.why: Highland knob near the edge of the plateau escarpment.
mountains.look: Dark knob behind Pale Wall Mountain's cliff.
mountains.near: Pale Wall Mountain, Wolfpen Mountain, Hollow Creek.
mountains.memorable: A clear view of all three granite domes in a line below.

mountains.name: Pale Wall Mountain
mountains.where: Southern edge of the highlands, west of Thunderhole Gorge
mountains.desc: A mountain whose south face is a sheer 230 m wall of white granite streaked with black lichen and seep stains.
mountains.why: Exfoliation joints parallel to the escarpment peel off huge sheets of granite.
mountains.look: A white wall visible from the sound and from Calder.
mountains.near: Glassface Dome, Thunderhole Gorge, the Whitlock Grade.
mountains.memorable: The largest single sheet of bare rock in the islands.

mountains.name: Ravenrock
mountains.where: Eastern highlands above Fallon
mountains.desc: A summit with a band of dark gneiss cliffs where ravens and peregrine falcons nest.
mountains.why: Dark gneiss roof pendant over the granite, more resistant than the rock around it.
mountains.look: Dark rock band under a wooded summit.
mountains.near: Hornet Spire, Fallon Knob, Highlands Road.
mountains.memorable: Raven calls echoing off the cliff band.

mountains.name: Hawkbill Knob
mountains.where: Western end of the Whitlock Range above Hollow Reach
mountains.desc: A hooked summit ridge with a cliff facing Hollow Reach.
mountains.why: The range ends where Hollow Reach has cut it off.
mountains.look: A beak-shaped profile from the Gate Bridge.
mountains.near: Whitlock, Hollow Creek, Stillhouse Road.
mountains.memorable: Its silhouette looks like a hawk's bill.

mountains.name: Bald Rock
mountains.where: Central highlands between Thunderhole Gorge and Lantern Mountain
mountains.desc: A bare granite summit with weathering pits that fill with rainwater and a fringe of stunted pine.
mountains.why: Granite dome too steep and smooth for soil to hold.
mountains.look: A pale bald patch on a forested plateau.
mountains.near: Anvil Rock, Highlands Road, Thunderhole Gorge.
mountains.memorable: Rain pools in the granite reflect the sky.

mountains.name: Hornet Spire
mountains.where: Blue Wall edge west of the Bright Water Gorge
mountains.desc: A free-standing granite spire separated from the escarpment by a deep cleft.
mountains.why: Joint-controlled erosion has isolated a pillar of rock at the escarpment edge.
mountains.look: A pointed spire against the sky.
mountains.near: Bright Water Gorge, Anvil Rock, Highlands Road.
mountains.memorable: Visible from SR 64 as a needle above the forest.

mountains.name: Fallon Knob
mountains.where: Eastern end of the highlands above the Fallon Cliffs
mountains.desc: The last summit before the highlands meet the sea, with a view down onto Fallon harbour.
mountains.why: The highland block ends here at the coast.
mountains.look: Wooded knob above cliffs and harbour.
mountains.near: Fallon, Cape Fallon Light, Highlands Road.
mountains.memorable: You can look straight down onto fishing boats from 1,180 m.

mountains.name: Anvil Rock
mountains.where: Blue Wall edge south of Bald Rock
mountains.desc: A flat-topped prow of granite projecting from the escarpment edge, with a 300 m drop on three sides.
mountains.why: Resistant block at the escarpment edge undercut by the Blue Wall's retreat.
mountains.look: Anvil-shaped silhouette on the escarpment rim.
mountains.near: Bald Rock, Thunderhole Gorge, Grayback below.
mountains.memorable: The flat top is the most dramatic standing point on the Blue Wall.

mountains.name: Glassface Dome
mountains.where: Below the Blue Wall, east of Thunderhole Gorge
mountains.desc: A huge granite dome projecting from the escarpment face; its south side is a 350 m sheet of bare rock that streams with seep water.
mountains.why: Exfoliating granite pluton exposed as the escarpment retreated.
mountains.look: In winter, ice on the wet rock turns the face into a mirror.
mountains.near: Pale Wall Mountain, the Whitlock Grade, Thunderhole Falls.
mountains.memorable: The shining face is visible from the ferry crossing the sound.

mountains.name: Wolfpen Mountain
mountains.where: Western Graystone above the Gate Shelf
mountains.desc: A long, forested mountain that descends in steps toward Lookoff Mountain.
mountains.why: Ridge that steps down from the highlands to the Piedmont.
mountains.look: Forested staircase above the Blue Wall Road.
mountains.near: Lookoff Mountain, Gate Shelf, the Blue Wall Road.
mountains.memorable: A forested staircase from the cliff edge down to the sound.

mountains.name: Lookoff Mountain
mountains.where: South-western Graystone above Hollow Reach mouth
mountains.desc: A steep-sided mountain with a cleared overlook facing Calder.
mountains.why: Southern end of the Wolfpen ridge.
mountains.look: Wooded peak above the sound.
mountains.near: Hollow Reach, Blue Wall Road, Cassena Sound.
mountains.memorable: The overlook frames the Calder skyline across the water.

mountains.name: Grayback Mountain
mountains.where: Piedmont strip north-east of Graystone town
mountains.desc: A colossal bare granite dome rising 380 m from rolling farmland, with streaks of black lichen and pools of water on its summit.
mountains.why: A granite pluton more resistant than the surrounding schist, left standing as the land around it wore down.
mountains.look: A grey whale-back dome visible from everywhere on the south side of the island and from Calder.
mountains.near: Graystone, Quarry Creek, Bright Water Road, Cutstone.
mountains.memorable: The island is named for it.

mountains.name: Cutstone Mountain
mountains.where: West of Graystone town
mountains.desc: A granite hill half cut away by the Cutstone Quarry, leaving terraced grey benches and a flooded pit.
mountains.why: Fine-grained granite close to the harbour and the railroad.
mountains.look: Stepped grey benches on one side, forest on the other.
mountains.near: Cutstone, Cutstone Quarry Hole, Blue Wall Incline.
mountains.memorable: Half natural mountain, half quarry.

mountains.name: Graystone Head
mountains.where: South-east tip of Graystone at the mouth of Cassena Sound
mountains.desc: A rocky headland with low cliffs and a stubby white light tower.
mountains.why: Hard gneiss headland at the sound mouth.
mountains.look: Low cliffs with a light tower.
mountains.near: Bright Water mouth, Graystone Coast Road.
mountains.memorable: Ships turning into the sound pass close under it.

mountains.name: Iron Mountain
mountains.where: Red Hills, northern Bellamy
mountains.desc: A 118 m hill capped with iron-cemented sandstone, with red clay roadcuts and a stand of longleaf pine on top.
mountains.why: An ironstone cap protects the soft sands beneath from erosion.
mountains.look: Deep red clay banks on the roads around it.
mountains.near: Harlow, Chalk Pits, Sugarloaf Hill.
mountains.memorable: Locals call it a mountain; from the flat farm plain it looks like one.

mountains.name: Sugarloaf Hill
mountains.where: Red Hills, north of Lake Ocosta
mountains.desc: A steep, conical hill of red sand with a church and cemetery on its top.
mountains.why: An erosional remnant of the old upland surface.
mountains.look: Church steeple on a hilltop.
mountains.near: Lake Ocosta, Red Hills Road.
mountains.memorable: The steeple marks the hill for miles across the farmland.

mountains.name: Calder Heights
mountains.where: Centre of Calder Island
mountains.desc: A granite-gneiss ridge in the middle of the city, topped by a stone-walled reservoir and a broadcast tower.
mountains.why: The bedrock knob that made Calder island dry and defensible.
mountains.look: Green hill rising from the grid of streets.
mountains.near: Heights Reservoir, the Heights district, Midtown.
mountains.memorable: The highest ground in the city, with views of the harbour.

mountains.name: Scrub Hill
mountains.where: Sandhill Ridge, central Wickham
mountains.desc: The highest point on Wickham: a dune summit of white sand with sand pine scrub and a fire lookout tower.
mountains.why: An ancient dune ridge left by higher seas.
mountains.look: White sand patches among dark scrub.
mountains.near: Punchbowl Sink, the Ridge Road, Blue Sink.
mountains.memorable: Barefoot-white sand 76 m above the sea.

mountains.name: Fire Tower Hill
mountains.where: Southern Sandhill Ridge
mountains.desc: A sandy knob with an old steel fire tower and longleaf savanna.
mountains.why: Southern continuation of the relict dune ridge.
mountains.look: Fire tower above open pine savanna.
mountains.near: Deep Lake, Little Sink, Ridge Road.
mountains.memorable: The tower overlooks both coasts of Wickham.

mountains.name: Highpine Knoll
mountains.where: Long Ridge, eastern Ossahatchee
mountains.desc: A low summit on the dune ridge with a fire tower and tall longleaf pines.
mountains.why: The highest point of the relict barrier ridge that dams the swamp.
mountains.look: Tall pines above the swamp canopy.
mountains.near: Long Ridge Pond, Tarrow Landing, Coastal Highway.
mountains.memorable: From the tower the swamp looks like a green sea.

mountains.name: Kestrel Hill
mountains.where: Kestrel Island, Gannet Banks
mountains.desc: The tallest sand dune on the Atlantic coast of the archipelago: a migrating hill of bare sand 28 m high.
mountains.why: Wind-blown sand from a wide beach piles up where the barrier is widest.
mountains.look: Bare white dune rising above the village rooftops.
mountains.near: Kestrel, Kestrel Beach, Banks Highway.
mountains.memorable: People slide down it on cardboard and fly kites from the top.

districts.name: Downtown Calder
districts.desc: The central business district on the bluff at the river mouth: glass and limestone towers up to 64 storeys, the old customs house, and narrow streets laid out on the colonial grid.
districts.why: The first dry ground above the deep anchorage at the Tennalee mouth; land values here have always been the highest on the island.
districts.look: A tight cluster of towers on a bluff, the tallest crowned with a lit spire.
districts.near: Old Market, Station Square, Market Street Bridge, Calder Tower.
districts.memorable: The skyline rising straight out of the water when seen from the Tennalee River Bridge.

districts.name: Old Market
districts.desc: Three- and four-storey brick warehouses, cobbled streets and an open-sided market shed along the wharves.
districts.why: The original deep-water wharves below the bluff.
districts.look: Red brick, iron balconies and cobblestones.
districts.memorable: Cobbles glistening after summer storms.

districts.name: Calder Point
districts.desc: The oldest houses on the island, tall and narrow, behind a high seawall promenade and a park at the tip.
districts.why: The point at the junction of the North Channel and the Inner Harbor, the first place settled.
districts.look: Pastel facades along a curving seawall.
districts.near: Calder Harbor Light, Old Market, Harbor Bridge.
districts.memorable: Watching ships turn into the harbour from the seawall.

districts.name: Station Square
districts.desc: The district around Calder Central station, with its clock tower, hotels and the bus terminal.
districts.why: Where the passenger railroad crosses the Market Street Bridge into the city.
districts.look: A stone clock tower among mid-rise hotels.
districts.near: Calder Central, Downtown, Market Street Bridge.
districts.memorable: The station clock tower lit at night.

districts.name: Midtown
districts.desc: Office and apartment towers of the 1960s–2000s along the main avenue south of Downtown.
districts.why: The commercial spillover from Downtown along the interstate spur.
districts.look: Mid-rise blocks and a canyon of an avenue.
districts.memorable: Afternoon thunderstorms funnelling down the avenue.

districts.name: Uptown
districts.desc: Apartment towers along the North Channel shore with balconies facing the mountains.
districts.why: North-facing waterfront with views of the Halcomb range.
districts.look: Towers with the North Face behind them.
districts.memorable: Mountains reflected in the channel.

districts.name: Northpoint
districts.desc: A neighbourhood of walk-up apartments and bungalows at the island's north-west corner.
districts.why: The flat end of the island beside the interstate bridge.
districts.look: Low streets under the bridge approach.
districts.memorable: Living under the bridge ramps.

districts.name: The Heights
districts.desc: Large Victorian and Colonial Revival houses on the granite ridge, with old oaks over the streets.
districts.why: The highest, coolest and best-drained ground in the city.
districts.look: Big houses and big trees on a hill.
districts.memorable: Oak canopy over brick-paved streets.

districts.name: Reservoir Hill
districts.desc: Terraced streets descending the south side of the ridge from the reservoir.
districts.why: Slopes of the Heights.
districts.look: Stepped streets and stairs.
districts.memorable: Public stairways between streets.

districts.name: Mill Creek
districts.desc: Rowhouses in the shallow valley of a creek now buried in a brick culvert; its stone outfall still opens onto the harbour.
districts.why: The only stream valley on the island, built over as the city grew.
districts.look: Rows of narrow brick houses on a curving street.
districts.memorable: The street follows the curve of the buried creek.

districts.name: Westside
districts.desc: Apartment buildings and townhouses along Westside Park and the bay shore.
districts.why: Sheltered west shore facing Serena Bay.
districts.look: Buildings framing the park.
districts.memorable: Sunsets over the bay from the park.

districts.name: Ellery Park
districts.desc: The city's great park around Lake Ellery: lawns, oak woods, cypress lake and a boathouse.
districts.why: Wet ground at a former tidal creek, never built on.
districts.look: Green against the grid.
districts.near: Lake Ellery, Westside, Westside Park Beach.
districts.memorable: Cypress trees in the middle of a city.

districts.name: Yacht Basin
districts.desc: Marinas, boat storage and waterfront restaurants on the south-west shore.
districts.why: Sheltered water on the lee side of the island.
districts.look: Masts and boat sheds.
districts.memorable: Forest of masts at sunset.

districts.name: South Shore
districts.desc: Apartments and houses along the seawall facing Saint Ambrose.
districts.why: South-facing shore across the narrow sound.
districts.look: Seawall promenade and palms.
districts.memorable: The Long Bridge hump at sunset.

districts.name: Southside
districts.desc: Warehouses, the wastewater plant and truck yards on reclaimed land.
districts.why: Low, filled land at the south-east corner.
districts.look: Flat roofs and tanks.
districts.near: Calder Southside Treatment Plant, Stadium District.
districts.memorable: The digester eggs of the treatment plant.

districts.name: Harborside
districts.desc: Old cotton and tobacco warehouses on the Inner Harbor converted to lofts and offices.
districts.why: The east shore facing Corliss, once the main freight wharves.
districts.look: Long brick warehouses with painted signs.
districts.memorable: Ghost signs on brick walls.

districts.name: Cotton Exchange
districts.desc: The old cotton exchange building and surrounding commercial blocks, now galleries and studios.
districts.why: The trading district behind the wharves.
districts.look: Ornate commercial facades.
districts.memorable: The exchange building's copper dome.

districts.name: Hospital Hill
districts.desc: Calder General Hospital and medical buildings on the east shoulder of the Heights.
districts.why: Built on high ground above the flood zone.
districts.look: White hospital towers with a helipad.
districts.memorable: Helicopters landing on the roof.

districts.name: University
districts.desc: The campus of Calder State University: brick quadrangles, live oaks and a bell tower.
districts.why: Quiet south-west part of the island.
districts.look: Bell tower over oak-shaded lawns.
districts.memorable: The bell tower above the trees.

districts.name: Stadium District
districts.desc: The football stadium and arena on filled land near the harbour.
districts.why: Large flat site on reclaimed land with highway access.
districts.look: The stadium bowl and its lights.
districts.memorable: Stadium lights glowing over the harbour on game nights.

districts.name: Cypress Row
districts.desc: Painted rowhouses with deep porches on a street lined with cypress planters.
districts.why: Old middle-class streets between the wharves and the Heights.
districts.look: Pastel rowhouses.
districts.memorable: A row of brightly painted porches.

districts.name: Brickyard
districts.desc: A former brickworks with kilns and chimneys now converted to lofts and studios.
districts.why: The clay pits along the ridge supplied brick for the old city.
districts.look: Beehive kilns and brick chimneys.
districts.memorable: Old kilns used as cafes.

districts.name: Gasworks
districts.desc: A district around the iron frame of an old gasholder, now a park and apartments.
districts.why: The old town gasworks by the water.
districts.look: A giant iron ring of the gasholder frame.
districts.memorable: The gasholder frame lit at night.

districts.name: Fairgrounds
districts.desc: The county fairgrounds and exposition hall with surrounding bungalows.
districts.why: Open ground on the south side of the island.
districts.look: Exhibition halls and a grandstand.
districts.memorable: The Ferris wheel at fair time.

districts.name: Ferry Landing
districts.desc: The ferry terminal for the Graystone ferry and the heliport pier.
districts.why: Deep water at the tip of the bluff.
districts.look: Ferry slips and a helipad pier.
districts.memorable: The ferry horn echoing off the towers.

districts.name: Tennalee Falls Mill District
districts.desc: Brick textile mills four and five storeys high along the river below the falls, with a tall chimney and a mill race.
districts.why: Water power at the fall line.
districts.look: Red brick mills beside white water.
districts.memorable: The falls roaring between the mills.

districts.name: Riverside
districts.desc: Barge wharves and working-class neighbourhoods on the terrace east of the river mouth.
districts.why: Low terrace at the river mouth facing downtown.
districts.look: Barges and frame houses.
districts.memorable: View of the downtown skyline across the channel.

districts.name: Halcomb Heights
districts.desc: Commuter suburbs on the foothill ridges above the North Channel.
districts.why: The first ridges beyond the bridge.
districts.look: Houses among trees on hills.
districts.memorable: Houses with mountain and city views.

districts.name: Falls Hill
districts.desc: Mill owners' houses on the hill above the falls.
districts.why: High ground overlooking the mills.
districts.look: Large houses on a wooded hill.
districts.memorable: Porches overlooking the falls.

districts.name: Tennalee Junction
districts.desc: The rail junction where the freight line to Corliss leaves the main line.
districts.why: The last land before the long lift bridge.
districts.look: Tracks, signals and freight cars.
districts.memorable: Freight trains lining up for the lift bridge.

districts.name: Corliss Town
districts.desc: Shotgun houses, bungalows and churches on the higher western end of the island.
districts.why: Housing within walking distance of the port and mills.
districts.look: Small houses under smokestacks.
districts.memorable: The mill whistle at shift change.

districts.name: Container Terminal
districts.desc: The container port: stacked boxes, straddle carriers and a row of ship-to-shore gantry cranes.
districts.why: Deep water on the north shore beside the ship channel.
districts.look: Giant cranes like mechanical giraffes.
districts.memorable: Crane booms raised against the sunset.

districts.name: Refinery Row
districts.desc: Tank farm, distillation columns and flare stacks of the refinery.
districts.why: Tanker berths and pipelines at the west end of the port.
districts.look: Tanks and towers lit like a city at night.
districts.memorable: The flare stack burning at night.

districts.name: Shipyard
districts.desc: Drydocks, slipways and a giant goliath crane at the east tip.
districts.why: Deep water at the island's east end.
districts.look: A goliath crane straddling a drydock.
districts.memorable: Ships in drydock with their hulls exposed.

districts.name: Bellamy Bluffs
districts.desc: Subdivisions and strip malls on the sandy bluffs south of the Long Bridge.
districts.why: Commuter access by I-21 and proximity to the airport.
districts.look: Cul-de-sacs among pines.
districts.memorable: Jets low over the rooftops.

districts.name: Airport Commerce Park
districts.desc: Warehouses and distribution centres along I-21 by the airport.
districts.why: Interstate, airport and port access.
districts.look: Huge flat-roofed buildings and truck docks.
districts.memorable: Lines of trucks at dawn.

districts.name: Courthouse Square
districts.desc: The domed county courthouse in a square of brick storefronts, with a water tower painted like a peanut.
districts.why: The centre of the farm county.
districts.look: Courthouse dome and peanut water tower.
districts.memorable: The peanut-shaped water tower.

districts.name: Depot District
districts.desc: Railroad depot, cotton gin, peanut shellers and a grain elevator.
districts.why: Where the railroad meets the farm roads.
districts.look: Grain elevator towering over the town.
districts.memorable: Cotton lint drifting in the air at harvest.

districts.name: The Strip
districts.desc: The beach road lined with motels, souvenir shops, seafood restaurants and mini golf.
districts.why: The resort grew along the beach road nearest the causeway.
districts.look: Neon signs and palms.
districts.memorable: Neon at night.

districts.name: Pier District
districts.desc: Boardwalk amusements, a Ferris wheel and arcades at the foot of the pier.
districts.why: The pier is the focus of the resort.
districts.look: Ferris wheel by the sea.
districts.memorable: The Ferris wheel lit at night.

districts.name: Condo Row
districts.desc: A wall of 20- to 30-storey condominium towers along the beach.
districts.why: Beachfront land at its most valuable.
districts.look: White towers in a line.
districts.memorable: Towers glowing pink at sunset.

districts.name: Port Serena Harbor
districts.desc: Marina, charter boats and seafood shacks on the lagoon side of the foreland.
districts.why: Sheltered lagoon water near the south bridge.
districts.look: Masts and docks.
districts.memorable: Charter boats unloading at dusk.

districts.name: Bay Street
districts.desc: The waterfront street of brick and tabby stores on the bluff, with a promenade over the river.
districts.why: The bluff-top landing on the deepest tidal river.
districts.look: Brick stores and live oaks over the river.
districts.near: Haversham Shrimp Docks, Bay Street Bluff.
districts.memorable: Moss hanging over the waterfront.

districts.name: The Point
districts.desc: Raised houses with deep porches and haint-blue ceilings on oak-shaded streets.
districts.why: High ground on the bluff north of Bay Street.
districts.look: Tall raised houses under live oaks.
districts.memorable: Houses raised high above floodwaters.

districts.name: Shrimp Docks
districts.desc: Shrimp boats with their outriggers raised, ice houses and net lofts.
districts.why: Deep water close to the bluff.
districts.look: Outriggers and nets.
districts.memorable: Boats unloading at dawn.

districts.name: Uptown Haversham
districts.desc: Newer commercial streets and churches back from the river, with three white steeples.
districts.why: The town's growth inland from the bluff.
districts.look: Three steeples over the rooftops.
districts.memorable: The steeples visible from the marsh.

districts.name: Graystone Harbor
districts.desc: Granite-built harbour town with the ferry terminal and stone wharves.
districts.why: The sheltered south-facing harbour.
districts.look: Grey granite buildings by the water.
districts.memorable: Grayback towering over the harbour.

districts.name: Fallon Harbor
districts.desc: Houses stacked up the cove walls around the fishing harbour.
districts.why: The only break in the cliffs.
districts.look: Colourful houses climbing the cliffs.
districts.memorable: Houses on steps above the boats.

districts.name: Ledford Parkway Strip
districts.desc: Pancake houses, motels, an aerial tramway and an observation tower along the Gap Road at the foot of the mountains.
districts.why: Gateway where the Gap Road leaves the foothills.
districts.look: Billboards and a needle-like observation tower.
districts.memorable: The tramway cars swinging up the mountainside.

districts.name: Narrows Landing
districts.desc: A bridgehead town of motels, gas stations and an old ferry landing under the Narrows Bridge.
districts.why: Where the bridge lands from the mainland.
districts.look: The bridge steelwork above the town.
districts.memorable: The bridge looming over Main Street.
